It is most likely that this Psalm was composed in this way, and this, as well as its acrostical arrangement, will account for its general want of connection. <div eID="gen22749" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22750" type="x-p"/> Though the most judicious interpreters assign it to the times of the Babylonish captivity; yet there are so many things in it descriptive of David's state, experience, and affairs, that I am led to think it might have come from his pen; or if composed at or under the captivity, was formed out of his notes and memoranda. <div eID="gen22750" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22751" type="x-p"/> I shall now make short remarks on the principal subjects in each part; and, at the end of each, endeavor by the Analysts to show the connection which the eight verses of each have among themselves, and the use which the reader should make of them. In all the Versions except the Chaldee this Psalm is numbered 118. <div eID="gen22751" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22752" type="x-p"/> <hi type="bold">Verse 1</hi> <div eID="gen22752" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22753" type="x-p"/> Blessed are the undefiled in the way - אשרי תמימי דרך ashrey temimey darech, "O the blessedness of the perfect ones in the way." This Psalm begins something like the first, where see the notes <reference osisRef="Psa.1.1-Psa.1.6">Psa 1:1-6</reference> (note). By the perfect, which is the proper meaning of the original word, we are to undertsand those who sincerely believe what God has spoken, religiously observe all the rules and ceremonies of his religion, and have their lives and hearts regulated by the spirit of love, fear, and obedience. This is farther stated in the second verse.
entries.9fd7f8ce30ec5bfa73a5838b5549a5d62db28057: <hi type="bold">Verse 3</hi> <div eID="gen22753" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22754" type="x-p"/> They also do no iniquity - They avoid all idolatry, injustice, and wrong; and they walk in God's ways, not in those ways to which an evil heart might entice them, nor those in which the thoughtless and the profligate tread.
entries.014757fba2800323336687882cbd34ede0c84b35: <hi type="bold">Verse 4</hi> <div eID="gen22754" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22755" type="x-p"/> Thy precepts diligently - מאד meod, "superlatively, to the uttermost." God has never given a commandment, the observance of which he knew to be impossible. And to whatsoever he has commanded he requires obedience; and his grace is sufficient for us. We must not trifle with God.
entries.7760f559d6a3d282e5151976519ff4782447a1a8: <hi type="bold">Verse 5</hi> <div eID="gen22755" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22756" type="x-p"/> O that my ways were directed - "I wish that my way may be confirmed to keep thy statutes." Without thee I can do nothing; my soul is unstable and fickle; and it will continue weak and uncertain till thou strengthen and establish it.
entries.d4b9a501c3aa44d214465ff623e252f568abb432: <hi type="bold">Verse 6</hi> <div eID="gen22756" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22757" type="x-p"/> Then shall I not be ashamed - Every act of transgression in the wicked man tends to harden his heart; and render it callous. If a man who fears God is so unhappy as to fall into sin, his conscience reproaches him, and he is ashamed before God and man. This is a full proof that God's Spirit has not utterly departed from him, and that he may repent, believe and be healed. <div eID="gen22757" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22758" type="x-p"/> Unto all thy commandments - God requires universal obedience, and all things are possible to him whom Christ strengthens; and all things are possible to him that believes. Allow that any of God's commandments may be transgressed, and we shall soon have the whole decalogue set aside.
entries.0474db349b3b58d1f8799fe7231c95137747c2cd: <hi type="bold">Verse 8</hi> <div eID="gen22758" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22759" type="x-p"/> O forsake me not utterly - עד מאד ad meod, "to utter dereliction;" never leave me to my own strength, nor to my own heart!
entries.271a6734b4cc1497d10d64ee1f1cea10320f9124: <hi type="bold">Verse 9</hi> <div eID="gen22759" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22760" type="x-p"/> A young man cleanse his way - ארח orach, which we translate way here, signifies a track, a rut, such as is made by the wheel of a cart or chariot. A young sinner has no broad beaten path; he has his private ways of offense, his secret pollutions: and how shall he be cleansed from these? how can he be saved from what will destroy mind, body, and soul? Let him hear what follows; the description is from God. <div eID="gen22760" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22761" type="x-p"/> 1. He is to consider that his way is impure; and how abominable this must make him appear in the sight of God. <div eID="gen22761" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22762" type="x-p"/> 2. He must examine it according to God's word, and carefully hear what God has said concerning him and it. <div eID="gen22762" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22763" type="x-p"/> 3. He must take heed to it, לשמר lishmor, to keep guard, and preserve his way - his general course of life, from all defilement.
entries.669db4c6c8b35344a159e6ed2ec10e91b0e03e3a: <hi type="bold">Verse 10</hi> <div eID="gen22763" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22764" type="x-p"/> With my whole heart have I sought thee - <div eID="gen22764" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22765" type="x-p"/> 4. He must seek God, make earnest prayer and supplication to him for Divine light, for a tender conscience, and for strength to walk uprightly. <div eID="gen22765" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22766" type="x-p"/> 5. His whole heart; all his affections must be engaged here, or he cannot succeed. If he keep any affection for the idol or abomination; if his heart do not give it before the Lord, he may make many prayers, but God will answer none of them. <div eID="gen22766" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22767" type="x-p"/> 6. He must take care to keep in the path of duty, of abstinence and self-denial; not permitting either his eye, his hand, or his heart to wander from the commandments of his Maker.
entries.233ee5274596355081bbdaef1c2e4a52765b07a5: <hi type="bold">Verse 11</hi> <div eID="gen22767" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22768" type="x-p"/> Thy word have I hid in my heart - <div eID="gen22768" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22769" type="x-p"/> 7. He must treasure up those portions of God's word in his mind and heart which speak against uncleanness of every kind; and that recommend purity, chastity, and holiness. The word of Christ should dwell richly in him. If God's word be only in his Bible, and not also in his heart, he may soon and easily be surprised into his besetting sin.
entries.dadaf507aa6d587d0bcaeed8f887d56af7f4d1b2: <hi type="bold">Verse 12</hi> <div eID="gen22769" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22770" type="x-p"/> Blessed art thou - <div eID="gen22770" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22771" type="x-p"/> 8. He must acknowledge the mercy of God, in so far preserving him from all the consequences of his sin. <div eID="gen22771" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22772" type="x-p"/> 9. He should beg of him to become his teacher that his heart and conscience might be instructed in the spirituality of his statutes.
entries.e17d120f9ee56ada76ea6b565752e473d3fe3282: <hi type="bold">Verse 13</hi> <div eID="gen22772" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22773" type="x-p"/> With my lips have I declared - <div eID="gen22773" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22774" type="x-p"/> 10. He should declare to his own heart, and to all his companions in iniquity, God's judgments against himself and them; that if his longsuffering merely have not made a proper impression on their hearts, they may tremble at his approaching judgments.
entries.5bb520f4819e72251a64c9fcdad1b9f6ed0c1c1e: <hi type="bold">Verse 14</hi> <div eID="gen22774" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22775" type="x-p"/> I have rejoiced - <div eID="gen22775" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22776" type="x-p"/> 11. He must consider it his chief happiness to be found in the path of obedience, giving his whole heart and strength to God; and when enabled to do it, he should rejoice more in it than if he had gained thousands of gold and silver. O how great is the treasure of a tender and approving conscience!
entries.ce62cac3f29b3a73841947abdbc113b78d420df3: <hi type="bold">Verse 15</hi> <div eID="gen22776" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22777" type="x-p"/> I will meditate - <div eID="gen22777" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22778" type="x-p"/> 12. He should encourage self-examination and reflection; and meditate frequently on God's words, works, and ways - and especially on his gracious dealings towards him. <div eID="gen22778" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22779" type="x-p"/> 13. He should keep his eye upon God's steps; setting the example of his Savior before his eyes, going where he would go, and nowhere else; doing what he would do, and nothing else; keeping the company that he would keep, and none else; and doing every thing in reference to the final judgment.
entries.22c6c84b8933a73389b19621a6d7097cdfff12da: <hi type="bold">Verse 16</hi> <div eID="gen22779" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22780" type="x-p"/> I will delight myself - The word is very emphatical: אשתעשע eshtaasha, I will skip about and jump for joy. <div eID="gen22780" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22781" type="x-p"/> 14. He must exult in God's word as his treasure, live in the spirit of obedience as his work, and ever glory in God, who has called him to such a state of salvation. <div eID="gen22781" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22782" type="x-p"/> 15. He must never forget what God has done for him, done in him, and promised farther to do; and he must not forget the promises he had made, and the vows of the Lord that are upon him. Any young man who attends to these fifteen particulars will get his impure way cleansed; victory over his sin; and, if he abide faithful to the Lord that bought him, an eternal heaven at last among them that are sanctified.
entries.13b5fe791948e9cb131fcb8b13f08ae0c1408e7b: <hi type="bold">Verse 17</hi> <div eID="gen22782" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22783" type="x-p"/> Deal bountifully - גמל gemol, reward thy servant. Let him have the return of his faith and prayers, that the Divine life may be preserved in his soul! Then he will keep thy word. From גמל gamal, to reward, etc., comes the name of ג gimel, the third letter in the Hebrew alphabet, which is prefixed to every verse in this part, and commences it with its own name. This is a stroke of the psalmist's art and ingenuity.
entries.3b9435ce73348f523da9984ff6f952a5676a8fb2: <hi type="bold">Verse 18</hi> <div eID="gen22783" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22784" type="x-p"/> Open thou mine eyes - גל עיני gal eynai, reveal my eyes, illuminate my understanding, take away the veil that is on my heart, and then shall I see wonders in thy law. The Holy Scriptures are plain enough; but the heart of man is darkened by sin. The Bible does not so much need a comment, as the soul does the light of the Holy Spirit. Were it not for the darkness of the human intellect, the things relative to salvation would be easily apprehended.
entries.79c0ea0f67eb0ce8ff6a12c652cac2c7016ffa1d: <hi type="bold">Verse 19</hi> <div eID="gen22784" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22785" type="x-p"/> I am a stranger in the earth - In the land. Being obliged to wander about from place to place, I am like a stranger even in my own country. If it refer to the captives in Babylon, it may mean that they felt themselves there as in a state of exile; for, although they had been seventy years in it, they still felt it as a strange land, because they considered Palestine their home.
entries.1f971c6c1e0aafd45ee01588406ee45eaddf44ab: <hi type="bold">Verse 20</hi> <div eID="gen22785" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22786" type="x-p"/> My soul breaketh - We have a similar expression: It broke my heart, That is heart-breaking, She died of a broken heart. It expresses excessive longing, grievous disappointment, hopeless love, accumulated sorrow. By this we may see the hungering and thirsting which the psalmist had after righteousness, often mingled with much despondency.
entries.78358c5329f9de0ce2f505e4c9ada03295884c30: <hi type="bold">Verse 21</hi> <div eID="gen22786" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22787" type="x-p"/> Thou hast rebuked the proud - This was done often in the case of David; and was true also in reference to the Babylonians, who held the Israelites in subjection, and whose kings were among the proudest of human beings. Instead of זדים zedim, the proud, some MSS. read זרים zarim, strangers, and one reads גוים goyim, the heathen; and so the Syriac.
entries.9f1ad74d9b16f217e61f6a845b22a56eaeb20db1: <hi type="bold">Verse 22</hi> <div eID="gen22787" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22788" type="x-p"/> Remove from me reproach and contempt - Of these the captives in Babylon had a more than ordinary load.
entries.ce3cb3d7fd8af5d0db19cdccc315785c48e09a9e: <hi type="bold">Verse 23</hi> <div eID="gen22788" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22789" type="x-p"/> Princes also did sit - It is very likely that the nobles of Babylon did often, by wicked misrepresentations, render the minds of the kings of the empire evil affected towards the Jews.
entries.db2faaac94645c2f4eb5c3ae5dd2c3a4135da891: <hi type="bold">Verse 24</hi> <div eID="gen22789" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22790" type="x-p"/> Thy testimonies also are - my counsellors - אנשי עצתי anshey atsathi, "the men of my counsel." I sit with them; and I consider every testimony thou hast given as a particular counsellor; one whose advice I especially need. <div eID="gen22790" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22791" type="x-p"/> The Analysis will farther explain the particular uses of this part.
entries.a213da349ac80986922a603ba52872995db582de: <hi type="bold">Verse 25</hi> <div eID="gen22791" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22792" type="x-p"/> My soul cleaveth unto the dust - It would be best to translate נפשי naphshi, my life; and then cleaving to the dust may imply an apprehension of approaching death; and this agrees best with the petition. <div eID="gen22792" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22793" type="x-p"/> Quicken thou me - חיני chaiyeni, "make me alive." Keep me from going down into the dust.
entries.25348c0705dc3942d4a08f0febfeccbc1e3460e1: <hi type="bold">Verse 26</hi> <div eID="gen22793" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22794" type="x-p"/> I have declared my ways - ספרתי sipparti, "I have numbered my ways," I have searched them out; I have investigated them. And that he had earnestly prayed for pardon of what was wrong in them, is evident; for he adds, "Thou heardest me."
entries.497e146a4cbd0924bc027804376894439343a27a: <hi type="bold">Verse 28</hi> <div eID="gen22794" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22795" type="x-p"/> My soul melteth - דלף dalaph sigifies to distil, to drop as tears from the eye. As my distresses cause the tears to distil from my eyes, so the overwhelming load of my afflictions causes my life to ebb and leak out.
entries.51068519ab0c3c69238232a64c3b31ea12552628: <hi type="bold">Verse 29</hi> <div eID="gen22795" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22796" type="x-p"/> The way of lying - The propensity to falsity and prevarication, whatsoever is contrary to truth. Remove me from its solicitations, and remove it from me. "Grant me thy law graciously;" give it to me as a rule of moral conduct; but give it to me graciously through the gospel, and then it will not be the letter that killeth, but will be sanctified to me, so as to become to me holy, just, and Good.
entries.6a165dfb356cdb0530d46d1ae959f290eb6f0dd0: <hi type="bold">Verse 30</hi> <div eID="gen22796" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22797" type="x-p"/> I have chosen the way of truth - And that I may continue in its "remove from me the way of lying." See above.
entries.9fac7d2a4d7ce4f0d97359385d02de2da547148a: <hi type="bold">Verse 31</hi> <div eID="gen22797" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22798" type="x-p"/> I have stuck - דבקתי dabakti, I have cleaved to, been glued to, them: the same word as in <reference osisRef="Psa.119.25">Psa 119:25</reference>. My soul cleaves as much to thy testimonies, as my life has cleaved to the dust. <div eID="gen22798" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22799" type="x-p"/> O Lord, put me not to shame - Let my sins and follies be blotted out by thy mercy; and so hide and cover them that they shall never appear, either in this or the coming world, to my shame and confusion! How many need to be importunate with God in this prayer!
entries.8cb7ce53d3bdad133565f7e1ea21cfd50f5ad6ec: <hi type="bold">Verse 32</hi> <div eID="gen22799" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22800" type="x-p"/> I will run - The particle כי elci, which we translate when, should be translated because: Because thou shalt enlarge, or dilate, my heart; make plain my path by cleansing me from my impurity, and taking the hinderances out of my way. I will then run without dread of stumbling, and every day make sensible progress.
entries.5e5913053206d8e2ba681c14dfb836a86a51dfe3: <hi type="bold">Verse 33</hi> <div eID="gen22800" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22801" type="x-p"/> Teach me, O Lord, the way of thy statutes - To understand the spiritual reference of all the statutes, etc, under the law, required a teaching which could only come from God. <div eID="gen22801" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22802" type="x-p"/> I shall keep it unto the end - Here is a good thing asked for a good end. He wishes for heavenly teaching; not to make a parade of it, but to enable him to discern his duty, that he might act accordingly.
entries.769256b5b670647a26235d98374b9899d968652e: <hi type="bold">Verse 34</hi> <div eID="gen22802" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22803" type="x-p"/> With my whole heart - I will not trifle with my God, I will not divide my affections with the world; God shall have all.
entries.034960afbe2dd54df5c152fac2f4ffe22dbe20a6: <hi type="bold">Verse 36</hi> <div eID="gen22803" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22804" type="x-p"/> Not to covetousness - Let me have no inordinate love for gain of any kind, nor for any thing that may grieve thy Spirit, or induce me to seek my happiness here below.
entries.2c8c98e377afac2f85afc7ffc86092f597e542cc: <hi type="bold">Verse 37</hi> <div eID="gen22804" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22805" type="x-p"/> From beholding vanity - An idol, worldly pleasure, beauty, finery; any thing that is vain, empty, or transitory. Let me not behold it; let me not dwell upon it. Let me remember Achan: he saw, - he coveted, - he took, - he hid his theft, and was slain for his sin.
entries.95f59c732fb964cfe17a9f083553d17d4d0177d8: <hi type="bold">Verse 38</hi> <div eID="gen22805" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22806" type="x-p"/> Stablish thy word - Fulfil the promises thou hast made to me.
entries.8132839822de9930cb44c5ee96413b7efd860f51: <hi type="bold">Verse 39</hi> <div eID="gen22806" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22807" type="x-p"/> Turn away my reproach, which I fear - This may be understood of the reproach which a man may meet with in consequence of living a godly life, for such a life was never fashionable in any time or country. But I have found the following note on the passage: "I have done a secret evil; my soul is sorry for it: if it become public, it will be a heavy reproach to me. O God, turn it away, and let it never meet the eye of man!" - Anon.
entries.a3a6f6c172531d1c5418593651b26365128e5105: <hi type="bold">Verse 40</hi> <div eID="gen22807" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22808" type="x-p"/> Behold, I have longed - Thou searchest the heart; thou knowest that I have long desired thy salvation; thou seest that this desire still remains. Behold it! it is thy work; and through thy mercy I breathe after thy mercy. <div eID="gen22808" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22809" type="x-p"/> Quicken me - I am dying; O give me the spirit of life in Christ Jesus!
entries.b2dcb73d83c5c897a50552bd1ec1bb89c4648154: <hi type="bold">Verse 41</hi> <div eID="gen22809" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22810" type="x-p"/> Let thy mercies come - Let me speedily see the accomplishment of all my prayers! Let me have thy salvation - such a deliverance as it becomes thy greatness and goodness to impart. Let it be according to thy word - thy exceeding great and precious promises.
entries.85faa7fa1a457d6a3a8c51cac7b274f566538052: <hi type="bold">Verse 42</hi> <div eID="gen22810" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22811" type="x-p"/> So shall I have wherewith to answer - Many say, "My hope in thy mercy is vain;" but when thou fulfillest thy promises to me, then shall I answer to the confusion of their infidelity.
entries.24cdab9edbf5cd55377fb2d2547174792f933369: <hi type="bold">Verse 43</hi> <div eID="gen22811" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22812" type="x-p"/> Take not the word of truth - Grant that the assurances which thy prophets have given to the people of approaching deliverance may not fall to the ground; let it appear that they have spoken thy mind, and that thou hast fulfilled their word.
entries.378fee60a2d8de4d4aff0be5808b7400bd0ebb46: <hi type="bold">Verse 45</hi> <div eID="gen22812" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22813" type="x-p"/> I will walk at liberty - When freed from the present bondage, we shall rejoice in obedience to thy testimonies; we shall delight to keep all thy ordinances.
entries.73871403245ad20f5f925d0912037117101bfa2e: <hi type="bold">Verse 46</hi> <div eID="gen22813" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22814" type="x-p"/> I will speak - before kings - Dr. Delaney supposes that this is spoken in reference to Achish, king of Gath, whom David had instructed in the Jewish religion; but we have already seen that it is most likely that the Psalm was compiled under the Babylonish captivity. But the words may with more propriety be referred to the case of Daniel, and other bold and faithful Israelites, who spoke courageously before Nebuchadnezzar, Belshazzar, and Darius. See the books of Daniel, Ezra, and Nehemiah.
entries.d33767617261a0ff8f1a0e0f1a1fc831014c7368: <hi type="bold">Verse 47</hi> <div eID="gen22814" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22815" type="x-p"/> Thy commandments, which I have loved - O shame to Christians who feel so little affection to the Gospel of Christ, when we see such cordial, conscientious, and inviolate attachment in a Jew to the laws and ordinances of Moses, that did not afford a thousandth part of the privileges!
entries.495b7415ea0b63fd41067c7b4877005b28b4aa4a: <hi type="bold">Verse 48</hi> <div eID="gen22815" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22816" type="x-p"/> My hands also will I lift up - I will present every victim and sacrifice which the law requires. I will make prayer and supplication before thee, lifting up holy hands without wrath and doubting.
entries.b2e5d3a0475ed7efc44dd31ed37ec97a91287daa: <hi type="bold">Verse 49</hi> <div eID="gen22816" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22817" type="x-p"/> Remember the word - Thou hast promised to redeem us from our captivity; on that word we have built our hope. Remember that thou hast thus promised, and see that we thus hope.
entries.5b44dfae8c41219f9ae9a69ce8784e3b8be1a773: <hi type="bold">Verse 50</hi> <div eID="gen22817" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22818" type="x-p"/> This is my comfort - While enduring our harsh captivity, we anticipated our enlargement; and thy word of promise was the means of keeping our souls alive.
entries.1eccf46df14da681c86915c5c9e1d67e6ed79bd4: <hi type="bold">Verse 51</hi> <div eID="gen22818" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22819" type="x-p"/> The proud have had me - We have been treated, not only with oppressive cruelty, but also with contempt, because we still professed to trust in thee, the living God, who because of our transgressions hadst been greatly displeased with us; jet we have not declined from thy law.
entries.d78bffc73bed61dbcd613f19c724576dc0f7c91d: <hi type="bold">Verse 52</hi> <div eID="gen22819" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22820" type="x-p"/> I remembered thy judgments of old - The word judgments is here taken for providential dealing; and indeed kind treatment; that which God showed to the Hebrews in bearing with and blessing them. And it was the recollection of these judgments that caused him to comfort himself.
entries.dc1375ac4e6179417e1b6ce03f218d15b487dcea: <hi type="bold">Verse 53</hi> <div eID="gen22820" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22821" type="x-p"/> Horror hath taken hold upon me - The word זלעפה zilaphah, which we render horror, is thought to signify the pestilential burning wind called by the Arabs simoom. Here it strongly marks the idea that the psalmist had of the destructive nature of sin; it is pestilential; it is corrupting, mortal.
entries.62792c089bfb568cedc455e17810bebb426ff335: <hi type="bold">Verse 54</hi> <div eID="gen22821" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22822" type="x-p"/> Thy statutes have been my songs - During our captivity all our consolation was derived from singing thy praises, and chanting among our fellow-captives portions of thy law, and the precepts it contains.
entries.c579de078536d47e82a893a5bee9a48441a8cfd8: <hi type="bold">Verse 55</hi> <div eID="gen22822" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22823" type="x-p"/> I have remembered thy name - Thou art Jehovah; and as our God thou hast made thyself known unto us. In the deepest night of our affliction this has consoled me.
entries.a49d05d700a3f91f10fdb670867ff87934bc365d: <hi type="bold">Verse 56</hi> <div eID="gen22823" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22824" type="x-p"/> This I had, because I kept thy precepts - Though thou didst leave us under the power of our enemies, yet thou hast not left us without the consolations of thy Spirit.
entries.2b521ccac450668e205b195ce8a85e0304b298c4: <hi type="bold">Verse 57</hi> <div eID="gen22824" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22825" type="x-p"/> Thou art my portion, O Lord - From the fifty-seventh to the sixtieth verse may be seen the progress of the work of grace on the human heart, from the first dawn of heavenly light till the soul is filled with the fullness of God. But as I consider this Psalm as notes selected from diaries of past experience, formed at different times; and that the author has been obliged, for the support of his acrostic plan, to interchange circumstances, putting that sometimes behind which in the order of grace comes before; because, to put it in its right place, the letters would not accord with the alphabetical arrangement; I shall therefore follow what I conceive to be its order in the connection of grace, and not in the order in which the words are here laid down.
entries.64bb0b8664c07256568d0348d4a3917d9c33bf09: <hi type="bold">Verse 59</hi> <div eID="gen22825" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22826" type="x-p"/> First. I thought on my ways - חשבתי chashabti, I deeply pondered them; I turned them upside down; I viewed my conduct on all sides. The word, as used here, is a metaphor taken from embroidering, where the figure must appear the same on the one side as it does on the other; therefore, the cloth must be turned on each side every time the needle is set in, to see that the stitch be fairly set. Thus narrowly and scrupulously did the psalmist examine his conduct; and the result was, a deep conviction that he had departed from the way of God and truth. <div eID="gen22826" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22827" type="x-p"/> Secondly. And turned my feet unto thy testimonies - Having made the above discovery, and finding himself under the displeasure of God, he abandoned every evil way, took God's word for his directory, and set out fairly in the way of life and salvation.
entries.05857f96c2100ac29609f73afffb55d606e3c343: <hi type="bold">Verse 60</hi> <div eID="gen22827" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22828" type="x-p"/> Thirdly. I made haste, and delayed not - He did this with the utmost speed; and did not trifle with his convictions, nor seek to drown the voice of conscience. <div eID="gen22828" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22829" type="x-p"/> The original word, which we translate delayed not, is amazingly emphatical. ולא התמהמהתי velo hithmahmahti, I did not stand what-what-whating; or, as we used to express the same sentiment, shilly-shallying with myself: I was determined, and so set out. The Hebrew word, as well as the English, strongly marks indecision of mind, positive action being suspended, because the mind is so unfixed as not to be able to make a choice. <div eID="gen22829" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22830" type="x-p"/> <hi type="bold">Verse 58</hi> <div eID="gen22830" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22831" type="x-p"/> Fourthly. Being determined in his heart, he tells us, I entreated thy favor with my whole heart. He found he had sinned; that he needed mercy; that he had no time to lose; that he must be importunate; and therefore he sought that mercy with all his soul. <div eID="gen22831" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22832" type="x-p"/> Fifthly. Feeling that he deserved nothing but wrath, that he had no right to any good, he cries for mercy in the way that God had promised to convey it: "Be merciful unto me!" And to this he is encouraged only by the promise of God; and therefore prays, "Be merciful unto me According to thy Word." <div eID="gen22832" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22833" type="x-p"/> <hi type="bold">Verse 57</hi> <div eID="gen22833" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22834" type="x-p"/> Sixthly. To keep himself firm in his present resolutions, he binds himself unto the Lord. "I have said that I would keep thy words." Thy vows are upon me, and I must not add to my guilt by breaking them. <div eID="gen22834" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22835" type="x-p"/> Seventhly. He did not seek in vain; God reveals himself in the fullness of blessedness to him, so that he is enabled to exclaim, Thou art my portion, O Lord! My whole soul trusts in thee, my spirit rests supremely satisfied with thee. I have no other inheritance, nor do I desire any. Here then is the way to seek, the way to find, and the way to be happy. Other effects of this conversion may be seen below.
entries.bebf15c524e212693b50f8a3c71b9370409226b0: <hi type="bold">Verse 61</hi> <div eID="gen22835" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22836" type="x-p"/> The bands of the wicked have robbed me - חבלי chebley, the cables, cords, or snares of the wicked. They have hunted us like wild beasts; many they have taken for prey, and many they have destroyed.
entries.72488ab2fef8a7762b1607a4e5f127faa464feb7: <hi type="bold">Verse 62</hi> <div eID="gen22836" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22837" type="x-p"/> At midnight I will rise - We are so overpowered with a sense of thy goodness, that in season and out of season we will return thee thanks.
entries.59485131270f50c636b3cdaf6cce4f65e1dd0568: <hi type="bold">Verse 63</hi> <div eID="gen22837" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22838" type="x-p"/> I am a companion - This was the natural consequence of his own conversion; he abandoned the workers of iniquity, and associated with them that feared the Lord.
entries.fb21de8bd650a1642a77da34e18184ed2c4eb03f: <hi type="bold">Verse 64</hi> <div eID="gen22838" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22839" type="x-p"/> The earth is full of thy mercy - What an astonishing operation has the grace of God! In the midst of want, poverty, affliction, and bondage, it makes those who possess it happy! When Christ dwells in the heart by faith, we have nothing but goodness around us. Others may complain; but to us even the earth appears full of the mercy of the Lord.
entries.a46645c1e567e7b3dfa225fcb7d0dbc673d25b7f: <hi type="bold">Verse 65</hi> <div eID="gen22839" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22840" type="x-p"/> Thou hast dealt well with thy servant - Whatsoever thy word has promised, thou hast fulfilled. Every servant of God can testify that God has done him nothing but good, and therefore he can speak good of his name.
entries.a2c69c094e60a7de4e0b356fe7369b825b6b3015: <hi type="bold">Verse 66</hi> <div eID="gen22840" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22841" type="x-p"/> Teach me good judgment and knowledge - טוב טעם ודעי למדני tob taam vedaath lammnedeni. Teach me (to have) a good taste and discernment. Let me see and know the importance of Divine things, and give me a relish for them.
entries.801116c444a925d1238ecce3086a93443e20e619: <hi type="bold">Verse 67</hi> <div eID="gen22841" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22842" type="x-p"/> Before I was afflicted I went astray - Many have been humbled under affliction, and taught to know themselves and humble themselves before God, that probably without this could never have been saved; after this, they have been serious and faithful. Affliction sanctified is a great blessing; unsanctified, it is an additional curse.
entries.d292df5c33a1ca828f3ca5f371286a7e53ad4336: <hi type="bold">Verse 68</hi> <div eID="gen22842" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22843" type="x-p"/> Thou art good - And because thou art good, thou doest good; and because thou delightest to do good, teach me thy statutes.
entries.2b662743f9aa829bbe28e01deb12ae5205a29a05: <hi type="bold">Verse 69</hi> <div eID="gen22843" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22844" type="x-p"/> The proud have forged a lie - The poor captives in Babylon had their conduct and motives continually misrepresented, and themselves belied and calumniated.
entries.48d6a6c99487341d612e7159b17dfbf26d7c66ae: <hi type="bold">Verse 70</hi> <div eID="gen22844" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22845" type="x-p"/> Their heart is as fat as grease - They are egregiously stupid, they have fed themselves without fear; they are become flesh-brutalized, and given over to vile affections, and have no kind of spiritual relish: but I delight in thy law - I have, through thy goodness, a spiritual feeling and a spiritual appetite.
entries.08f82d4647c3a9ef8813dfd801f672a34156c397: <hi type="bold">Verse 71</hi> <div eID="gen22845" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22846" type="x-p"/> It is good for me that I have been afflicted - See on <reference osisRef="Psa.119.67">Psa 119:67</reference> (note).
entries.9bdbd4c12f7af614aaa30b323761b322612f3b33: <hi type="bold">Verse 72</hi> <div eID="gen22846" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22847" type="x-p"/> The law of thy mouth is better - Who can say this? Who prefers the law of his God, the Christ that bought him, and the heaven to which he hopes to go, when he can live no longer upon earth, to thousands of gold and silver? Yea, how many are there who, like Judas, sell their Savior even for thirty pieces of silver? Hear this, ye lovers of the world and of money! <div eID="gen22847" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22848" type="x-p"/> As the letter ט teth begins but few words, not forty, in the Hebrew language, there is less variety under this division than under any of the preceding.
entries.0b27338f6870e784c65209fea289673eb49ec3ab: <hi type="bold">Verse 73</hi> <div eID="gen22848" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22849" type="x-p"/> Thy hands have made me - Thou hast formed the mass out of which I was made; and fashioned me - thou hast given me that particular form that distinguishes me from all thy other creatures. <div eID="gen22849" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22850" type="x-p"/> Give me understanding - As thou hast raised me above the beasts that perish in my form and mode of life, teach me that I may live for a higher and nobler end, in loving, serving, and enjoying thee for ever. Show me that I was made for heaven, not for earth.
entries.bc0277ebff8ac9a3d31966ae1b417b9b5d289b8c: <hi type="bold">Verse 74</hi> <div eID="gen22850" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22851" type="x-p"/> They that fear thee - They who are truly religious will be glad - will rejoice, at this farther proof of the saving power of God.
entries.c359ec0d9712268aebedf09f10d964a2a357afca: <hi type="bold">Verse 75</hi> <div eID="gen22851" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22852" type="x-p"/> I know - that thy judgments are right - All the dispensations of thy providence are laid in wisdom, and executed in mercy: let me see that it is through this wisdom and mercy that I have been afflicted.
entries.06465eb0ca4d9630753569d6b57eee814fb1b9c7: <hi type="bold">Verse 76</hi> <div eID="gen22852" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22853" type="x-p"/> Thy merciful kindness - Let me derive my comfort and happiness from a diffusion of thy love and mercy, חסדך chasdecha, thy exuberant goodness, through my soul.
entries.cbf6f7250167021a2d7c9818cf70f61f74957051: <hi type="bold">Verse 77</hi> <div eID="gen22853" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22854" type="x-p"/> Let thy tender mercies - רחמיך rachameycha, thy fatherly and affectionate feelings.
entries.f4cbc33d688ed5f2c0b467a8cf770f4a8d9568b5: <hi type="bold">Verse 78</hi> <div eID="gen22854" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22855" type="x-p"/> Let the proud be ashamed - To reduce a proud man to shame, is to humble him indeed. Let them be confounded. Without cause - without any colourable pretext, have they persecuted me.
entries.9ef22a49809a9551f552c3239173564ffc0c107e: <hi type="bold">Verse 79</hi> <div eID="gen22855" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22856" type="x-p"/> Let those that fear thee - The truly pious. <div eID="gen22856" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22857" type="x-p"/> Turn unto me - Seeing thy work upon me, they shall acknowledge me as a brand plucked from the burning.
entries.cabe650a6ced5416846bc54bcd7153a49e7c793e: <hi type="bold">Verse 80</hi> <div eID="gen22857" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22858" type="x-p"/> Let my heart be sound in thy statutes - Let it be perfect - all given up to thee, and all possessed by thee.
entries.8b8e5fe5ca2c22f2d9d0d5e97d4272d8cacc5e91: <hi type="bold">Verse 81</hi> <div eID="gen22858" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22859" type="x-p"/> My soul fainteth for thy salvation - I have longed so incessantly after thy salvation - the complete purification and restoration of my soul, that my very spirits are exhausted. "My heartstrings groan with deep complaint;My soul lies panting, Lord, for thee; <div eID="gen22859" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22860" type="x-p"/> And every limb and every jointStretches for perfect purity."
entries.b01e3aa12798a1518b82bf4ee9d6c7a5c6472d32: <hi type="bold">Verse 82</hi> <div eID="gen22860" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22861" type="x-p"/> Mine eyes fail - With looking up for the fulfillment of thy promise, as my heart fails in longing after thy presence.
entries.2999f2074ffb3357c35d517aee6140b202b27b26: <hi type="bold">Verse 83</hi> <div eID="gen22861" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22862" type="x-p"/> Like a bottle in the smoke - In the eastern countries their bottles are made of skins; one of these hung in the smoke must soon be parched and shrivelled up. This represents the exhausted state of his body and mind by long bodily affliction and mental distress.
entries.741074b973a511594fdb4ef55e723da31e5dadf2: <hi type="bold">Verse 84</hi> <div eID="gen22862" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22863" type="x-p"/> How many are the days of thy servants - Dost thou not know that I have few to live, and they are full of trouble? <div eID="gen22863" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22864" type="x-p"/> When wilt thou execute judgment on them that persecute me? - Shall not the pride of the Chaldeans be brought down, the arm of their strength broken, and thy people delivered? In this verse there is none of the ten words used in reference to God's law.
entries.def5151e87c2d529ce78fbd0672d20661c2ab9c3: <hi type="bold">Verse 85</hi> <div eID="gen22864" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22865" type="x-p"/> The proud have digged pits - The Vulgate, Septuagint, Ethiopic, and Arabic, translate this verse thus: "They have recited to me unholy fables, which are not according to thy law." They wish us to receive their system of idolatry, and the tales concerning their gods; but these are not according to thy law. The Anglo-Saxon is the same: They quothed me the unrightwise spells; but no so so law thine.
entries.99dddce92444c11d746352ce2a0cf09220e724e1: <hi type="bold">Verse 87</hi> <div eID="gen22865" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22866" type="x-p"/> They had almost consumed me - Had it not been for thy mercy, we had all been destroyed under this oppressive captivity.
entries.74c3790939fa9e5ea865b427da1246ed5bc2fbc4: <hi type="bold">Verse 88</hi> <div eID="gen22866" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22867" type="x-p"/> Quicken me - Make and keep me alive. <div eID="gen22867" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22868" type="x-p"/> So shall I keep - Without the spiritual life there is no obedience; we must therefore rise from the dead, and be quickened by the Spirit of Christ.
entries.c6b1ec27e7a6dc5a9451950ec9865c2cbe887180: <hi type="bold">Verse 89</hi> <div eID="gen22868" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22869" type="x-p"/> For ever, O Lord, thy word is settled in heaven - Thy purposes are all settled above, and they shall all be fulfilled below.
entries.64b8e206f1f55acb932a67b6a1468cb2cbdb4927: <hi type="bold">Verse 90</hi> <div eID="gen22869" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22870" type="x-p"/> Thy faithfulness - That which binds thee to accomplish the promise made. And this shall be, not for an age merely, but from generation to generation; for thy promises refer to the whole duration of time. <div eID="gen22870" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22871" type="x-p"/> Thou hast established the earth - Thou hast given it its appointed place in the system, and there it abideth.
entries.62a51b8e91d1937612f94219380ceb57e2234c99: <hi type="bold">Verse 91</hi> <div eID="gen22871" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22872" type="x-p"/> They continue this day - This verse should be thus read: All are thy servants; therefore, they continue this day according to thy ordinances. "All the celestial bodies are governed by thy power. Thou hast given an ordinance or appointment to each, and each fulfils thy will in the place thou hast assigned it."
entries.be4f68e65d3b2608412117079d50f578238f600e: <hi type="bold">Verse 92</hi> <div eID="gen22872" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22873" type="x-p"/> Unless thy law had been my delights - Had we not had the consolations of religion, we should long ago have died of a broken heart.
entries.21e7e5551e5738f23ab0d52c8b0c19b94139beec: <hi type="bold">Verse 93</hi> <div eID="gen22873" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22874" type="x-p"/> I will never forget thy precepts - How can I? It is by them I live.
entries.3224f2cc147b78cc4580e51429d8d9a70339574d: <hi type="bold">Verse 94</hi> <div eID="gen22874" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22875" type="x-p"/> I am thine, save me - He who can say this need fear no evil. In all trials, temptations, dangers, afflictions, persecutions, I am thine. Thy enemies wish to destroy me! Lord, look to thy servant; thy servant looks to thee. O how sovereign is such a word against all the evils of life! I am Thine! therefore save thine Own!
entries.74bdad6654863724a6dd30cb42c9a521fe3ebc55: <hi type="bold">Verse 96</hi> <div eID="gen22875" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22876" type="x-p"/> I have seen an end of all perfection - Literally, "Of all consummations I have seen the end:" as if one should say, Every thing of human origin has its limits and end, howsoever extensive, noble, and excellent. All arts and sciences, languages, inventions, have their respective principles, have their limits and ends; as they came from man and relate to man, they shall end with man: but thy law, thy revelation, which is a picture of thy own mind, an external manifestation of thy own perfections, conceived in thy infinite ideas, in reference to eternal objects, is exceeding broad; transcends the limits of creation; and extends illimitably into eternity! This has been explained as if it meant: All the real or pretended perfection that men can arrive at in this life is nothing when compared with what the law of God requires. This saying is false in itself, and is no meaning of the text. Whatever God requires of man he can, by his grace, work in man.
entries.8eae018bb068a1f2aa65b2f6ffcf2b2e64f4c1d9: <hi type="bold">Verse 97</hi> <div eID="gen22876" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22877" type="x-p"/> O how love I thy law - This is one of the strongest marks of a gracious and pious heart, cast in the mould of obedience. Such love the precepts of Christ: in his commandments they delight; and this delight is shown by their making them frequent subjects of their meditation.
entries.ab28ec2ce1b4d56ba82093e9fa96d6f7a4687dc3: <hi type="bold">Verse 98</hi> <div eID="gen22877" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22878" type="x-p"/> Wiser than mine enemies - Some have thought that this Psalm was composed by Daniel, and that he speaks of himself in these verses. Being instructed by God, he was found to have more knowledge than any of the Chaldeans, magicians, soothsayers, etc., etc.; and his wisdom soon appeared to the whole nation vastly superior to theirs.
entries.2acfdc833f286c01cf1ecb8dc267046f6c49785a: <hi type="bold">Verse 99</hi> <div eID="gen22878" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22879" type="x-p"/> I have more understanding than all my teachers - As he had entered into the spiritual nature of the law of God, and saw into the exceeding breadth of the commandment, he soon became wiser than any of the priests or even prophets who instructed him.
entries.87526af966dc8512e8c9bbf1a8c1372163806be5: <hi type="bold">Verse 100</hi> <div eID="gen22879" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22880" type="x-p"/> I understand more than the ancients - God had revealed to him more of that hidden wisdom which was in his law than he had done to any of his predecessors. And this was most literally true of David, who spoke more fully about Christ than any who had gone before him; or, indeed, followed after him. His compositions are, I had almost said, a sublime Gospel.
entries.b26bbce051206f77aea14bb3a47c621664829902: <hi type="bold">Verse 101</hi> <div eID="gen22880" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22881" type="x-p"/> I have refrained my feet - By avoiding all sin, the spirit of wisdom still continues to rest upon me.
entries.06bd1e3dce5a8f25531d77a13550e5390d5a9dd4: <hi type="bold">Verse 103</hi> <div eID="gen22881" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22882" type="x-p"/> Sweeter than honey to my mouth! - What deep communion must this man have had with his Maker! These expressions show a soul filled with God. O Christians, how vastly superior are our privileges! and alas! how vastly inferior in general, are our consolations, our communion with God, and our heavenly-mindedness!
entries.22706beeb19804413e01070acd8369eb9dcd2658: <hi type="bold">Verse 104</hi> <div eID="gen22882" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22883" type="x-p"/> Through thy precepts I get understanding - Spiritual knowledge increases while we tread in the path of obedience. Obedience is the grand means of growth and instruction. Obedience trades with the talent of grace, and thus grace becomes multiplied.
entries.b6ac53f6cd3425454c98168c7ff7d3fed4fc84f1: <hi type="bold">Verse 105</hi> <div eID="gen22883" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22884" type="x-p"/> Thy word is a lamp - This is illustrated thus by Solomon, <reference osisRef="Pro.6.23">Pro 6:23</reference> : "The commandment is a lamp; and the law is light; and reproofs of instruction are the way of life." God's word is a candle which may be held in the hand to give us light in every dark place and chamber; and it is a general light shining upon all his works, and upon all our ways.
entries.10db976ce453c1d543106a0ab8ef9cbb6e1553b5: <hi type="bold">Verse 106</hi> <div eID="gen22884" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22885" type="x-p"/> I have sworn - Perhaps this means no more than that he had renewed his covenant with God; he had bound himself to love and serve him only.
entries.73369bdebb2dec34e3100f8c3bff78fd84ba199f: <hi type="bold">Verse 107</hi> <div eID="gen22885" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22886" type="x-p"/> I am afflicted very much - עד מאד ad meod, "to extremity, excessively." We are in the most oppressive captivity. <div eID="gen22886" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22887" type="x-p"/> Quicken me - Deliver us from our bondage.
entries.e4f1995c5fc6c595e413652646e3f2adbf5a4668: <hi type="bold">Verse 108</hi> <div eID="gen22887" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22888" type="x-p"/> The freewill-offerings of my mouth - נדבות פי nidboth pi, the voluntary offerings which I have promised. Or, As we are in captivity, and cannot sacrifice to thee, but would if we could; accept the praises of our mouth, and the purposes of our hearts, instead of the sacrifices and offerings which we would bring to thy altar, but cannot.
entries.ea7cdb37b35e5554ba888daaf85a3e01b6cbaa8c: <hi type="bold">Verse 109</hi> <div eID="gen22888" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22889" type="x-p"/> My soul is continually in my hand - נפשי naphshi, my life; that is, it is in constant danger, every hour I am on the confines of death. <div eID="gen22889" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22890" type="x-p"/> The expression signifies to be in continual danger. So Xenarchus in Athenaeus, lib. xiii., c. 4: Εν τῃ χειρι την ψυχην εχοντα, "having the life in the hand;" which signifies continual danger and jeopardy. There is some thing like this in the speech of Achilles to Ulysses, Hom. Il. ix., ver. 322: - Αιει εμην ψυχην παραβαλλομενος πολεμιζειν· "Always presenting my life to the dangers of the fight." <div eID="gen22890" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22891" type="x-p"/> My soul is in thy hand, is the reading of the Syriac, Septuagint, Ethiopic, and Arabic; but this is a conjectural and useless emendation.
entries.829cc77bdc331732eadcac24dfe0038e7cbdf42d: <hi type="bold">Verse 110</hi> <div eID="gen22891" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22892" type="x-p"/> The wicked have laid a snare - Thus their lives were continually exposed to danger.
entries.d0ef26a0ab909412ae9b0b183b652bde12feedd8: <hi type="bold">Verse 111</hi> <div eID="gen22892" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22893" type="x-p"/> As a heritage - In <reference osisRef="Psa.119.57">Psa 119:57</reference> he says, God is my portion, חלקי chelki. In this he says, Thy testimonies have I taken as a heritage, נחל nachal. To these he was heir; he had inherited them from his fathers, and he was determined to leave them to his family for ever. If a man can leave nothing to his child but a Bible, in that he bequeaths him the greatest treasure in the universe.
entries.1388a8118144c3c39295f3e3efe6b2a3f6d19caf: <hi type="bold">Verse 112</hi> <div eID="gen22893" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22894" type="x-p"/> I have inclined mine heart - I used the power God gave me, and turned to his testimonies with all mine heart. When we work with God, we can do all things.
entries.77b3a81f62a9a9686439a2a63f4a35ee8e22d448: <hi type="bold">Verse 113</hi> <div eID="gen22894" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22895" type="x-p"/> I hate vain thoughts - I have hated סעפים seaphim, "tumultuous, violent men." I abominate all mobs and insurrections, and troublers of the public peace.
entries.ecb829082452cc4d701167fc03d9135a455be17e: <hi type="bold">Verse 114</hi> <div eID="gen22895" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22896" type="x-p"/> Mv hiding place - My asylum. <div eID="gen22896" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22897" type="x-p"/> And my shield - There is a time in which I may be called to suffer in secret; then thou hidest me. There may be a time in which thou callest me to fight; then thou art my Shield and Protector.
entries.6c97f18482c587844d0589ecbdaa18b4bee7fddf: <hi type="bold">Verse 116</hi> <div eID="gen22897" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22898" type="x-p"/> Depart from me - Odi profanum vulgus, etarceo, I abominate the profane, and will have no communion with them. I drive them away from my presence. <div eID="gen22898" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22899" type="x-p"/> Uphold me - סמכני sammecheni, prop me up; give me thyself to lean upon.
entries.14810198ab90c5c57708547fd678ebcbf36fe5ec: <hi type="bold">Verse 117</hi> <div eID="gen22899" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22900" type="x-p"/> Hold thou me up - I shall grow weary and faint in the way, if not strengthened and supported by thee. <div eID="gen22900" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22901" type="x-p"/> And I shall be safe - No soul can be safe, unless upheld by thee.
entries.b0d8e0871cfaa0f2042aac3859957f2b20fa1a95: <hi type="bold">Verse 118</hi> <div eID="gen22901" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22902" type="x-p"/> Thou hast trodden down - All thy enemies will be finally trodden down under thy feet. <div eID="gen22902" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22903" type="x-p"/> Their deceit is falsehood - Their elevation is a lie. The wicked often become rich and great, and affect to be happy, but it is all false; they have neither a clean nor approving conscience. Nor can they have thy approbation; and, consequently, no true blessedness.
entries.a83238fd73f37b0032836e8fee36a7d559d7f551: <hi type="bold">Verse 119</hi> <div eID="gen22903" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22904" type="x-p"/> Thou puttest away all the wicked of the earth like dross - There is no true metal in them: when they are tried by the refining fire, they are burnt up; they fly off in fumes, and come to no amount. There is probably an allusion here to the scum or scorias at the surface of melting metals, which is swept oft previously to casting the metal into the mould. <div eID="gen22904" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22905" type="x-p"/> Therefore I love thy testimonies - Thy testimonies will stand; and thy people will stand; because thou who didst give the one, and who upholdest the other, art pure, immovable, and eternal.
entries.ded3b9135625eafb5c37ffa574ed8e2f450b3c39: <hi type="bold">Verse 120</hi> <div eID="gen22905" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22906" type="x-p"/> My flesh trembleth for fear of thee - I know thou art a just and holy God: I know thou requirest truth in the inner parts. I know that thou art a Spirit, and that they who worship thee must worship thee in spirit and in truth; and I am often alarmed lest I fall short. It is only an assurance of my interest in thy mercy that can save me from distressing fears and harassing doubts. It is our privilege to know we are in God's favor; and it is not less so to maintain a continual filial fear of offending him. A true conception of God's justice and mercy begets reverence.
entries.8037772d2b616ae40a2d49a143bbec8f49df0edc: <hi type="bold">Verse 121</hi> <div eID="gen22906" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22907" type="x-p"/> I have done judgment and justice - I have given the best decision possible on every case that came before me; and I have endeavored to render to all their due.
entries.10a900724fde1669351fef1d3220baf37cab87fb: <hi type="bold">Verse 122</hi> <div eID="gen22907" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22908" type="x-p"/> Be surety for thy servant - ערב arob, give a pledge or token that thou wilt help me in times of necessity. Or, Be bail for thy servant. What a word is this! Pledge thyself for me, that thou wilt produce me safely at the judgment of the great day. Then sustain and keep me blameless till the coming of Christ. Neither of these two verses has any of the ten words in reference to God's law or attributes. The judgment and the justice refer to the psalmist's own conduct in <reference osisRef="Psa.119.121">Psa 119:121</reference>. The hundred and twenty-second has no word of the kind.
entries.f683b0881c5427b3d41f10bbe48b816882ad647d: <hi type="bold">Verse 123</hi> <div eID="gen22908" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22909" type="x-p"/> Mine eyes fail - See on <reference osisRef="Psa.119.82">Psa 119:82</reference> (note).
entries.bda0341b7484c326a664162ace7663950c6c2b82: <hi type="bold">Verse 125</hi> <div eID="gen22909" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22910" type="x-p"/> I am thy servant - See on <reference osisRef="Psa.119.94">Psa 119:94</reference> (note).
entries.efad9b25f60030a4ca460a84503c289f90436ebf: <hi type="bold">Verse 126</hi> <div eID="gen22910" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22911" type="x-p"/> It is time for thee, Lord, to work - The time is fulfilled in which thou hast promised deliverance to thy people. They - the Babylonians, <div eID="gen22911" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22912" type="x-p"/> Have made void thy law - They have filled up the measure of their iniquities.
entries.0203e3f0e4609196db85fd840c459b7e26808381: <hi type="bold">Verse 127</hi> <div eID="gen22912" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22913" type="x-p"/> Therefore I love thy commandments - I see thou wilt do all things well. I will trust in thee. <div eID="gen22913" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22914" type="x-p"/> Above gold - מזהב mizzahab, more than resplendent gold; gold without any stain or rust. <div eID="gen22914" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22915" type="x-p"/> Yea, above fine gold - ומפז umippaz, above solid gold; gold separated from the dross, perfectly refined.
entries.92afb12a007fd67edadbe5d604331a6a14b98bb3: <hi type="bold">Verse 128</hi> <div eID="gen22915" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22916" type="x-p"/> All thy precepts concerning all things to be right - There are too many supplied words here to leave the text unsuspected. All the ancient versions, except the Chaldee, seem to have omitted the second כל col, All and read the text thus: "Therefore I have walked straight in all thy precepts." I go straight on in all thy precepts, hating every false way. I neither turn to the right hand nor to the left; the false ways are crooked; thy way is straight. I am going to heaven, and that way lies straight before me. To walk in the way of falsity I cannot, because I hate it; and I hate such ways because God hates them.
entries.73aa8f34b203caf394ca3aeb46394e1e064768dd: <hi type="bold">Verse 129</hi> <div eID="gen22916" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22917" type="x-p"/> Thy testimonies are wonderful - There is a height, length, depth, and breadth in thy word and testimonies that are truly astonishing; and on this account my soul loves them, and I deeply study them. The more I study, the more light and salvation I obtain.
entries.790d168408ccdd5a127cd47c6338545a80765c9b: <hi type="bold">Verse 130</hi> <div eID="gen22917" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22918" type="x-p"/> The entrance of thy words giveth light - פתח pethach, the opening of it: when I open my Bible to read, light springs up in my mind. Every sermon, every prayer, every act of faith, is an opening by which light is let into the seeking soul.
entries.90c0a997ed78e2c46564d18326d3381332d3593f: <hi type="bold">Verse 131</hi> <div eID="gen22918" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22919" type="x-p"/> I opened my mouth, and panted - A metaphor taken from an animal exhausted in the chase. He runs, open-mouthed, to take in the cooling air; the heart beating high, and the muscular force nearly expended through fatigue. The psalmist sought for salvation, as he would run from a ferocious beast for his life. Nothing can show his earnestness in a stronger point of view.
entries.f2a5a8e940d7a561d6f5ac4d088ff7c02efbb0b3: <hi type="bold">Verse 132</hi> <div eID="gen22919" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22920" type="x-p"/> As thou usest to do - Treat me as thy mercy has induced thee to treat others in my circumstances. Deal with me as thou dealest with thy friends.
entries.135f158b7b7f0916ad7859bc6c89ceab14cf5820: <hi type="bold">Verse 133</hi> <div eID="gen22920" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22921" type="x-p"/> Order my steps - הכן hachen, make them firm; let me not walk with a halting or unsteady step. <div eID="gen22921" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22922" type="x-p"/> Have dominion over me - בי bi, In me. Let me have no governor but God, let the throne of my heart be filled by him, and none other.
entries.17a91e80cd95e5759b7772248d978b35511e0661: <hi type="bold">Verse 135</hi> <div eID="gen22922" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22923" type="x-p"/> Make thy face to shine - Give me a sense of thy approbation. Let me know, by the testimony of thy Spirit in my conscience, that thou art reconciled to me. The godly in all ages derived their happiness from a consciousness of the Divine favor. The witness of God's spirit in the souls of believers was an essential principle in religion from the foundation of the world.
entries.467e77cc991f3b183ab90d1c8f71e71a2dd43122: <hi type="bold">Verse 136</hi> <div eID="gen22923" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22924" type="x-p"/> Rivers of waters run down mine eyes - How much had this blessed man the honor of God and the salvation of souls at heart! O for more of that spirit which mourns for the transgressions of the land! But we are not properly convinced of the exceeding sinfulness of sin.
entries.aa55d6306bf5659ec40793e14b0080489cf9fbcc: <hi type="bold">Verse 137</hi> <div eID="gen22924" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22925" type="x-p"/> Righteous art thou - Thou art infinitely holy in thy nature; and therefore thou art upright in thy judgments - all thy dispensations to men.
entries.d10b3c0bf656d5e64a4742f54193c378e704aa27: <hi type="bold">Verse 138</hi> <div eID="gen22925" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22926" type="x-p"/> Thy testimonies - Every thing that proceeds from thee partakes of the perfections of thy nature.
entries.bd4f47129f10475e6e1ccd480e9cd3212a93a94e: <hi type="bold">Verse 139</hi> <div eID="gen22926" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22927" type="x-p"/> My zeal hath consumed me - My earnest desire to promote thy glory, and the pain I feel at seeing transgressions multiplied, have worn down both my flesh and spirits.
entries.93577322dfe8ed4ce24dc0ac10a5acf2d9261cb1: <hi type="bold">Verse 140</hi> <div eID="gen22927" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22928" type="x-p"/> Thy word is very pure - צרופה tseruphah, it is purification. It is not a purified thing, but a thing that purifies. "Now ye are clean," said Christ, "by the word I have spoken unto you." God's word is a fire to purify as well as a hammer to break.
entries.4ae169057a54663d6895e6bce4819e1685256cef: <hi type="bold">Verse 141</hi> <div eID="gen22928" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22929" type="x-p"/> I am small and despised - And on these accounts have every thing to fear. Being small, I cannot resist; being despised, I am in danger; but even all this does not induce me to start aside, or through the fear of man to be unfaithful to thee.
entries.eeca4aeb1219effd7d7009462a239c7d72c492c0: <hi type="bold">Verse 142</hi> <div eID="gen22929" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22930" type="x-p"/> Thy righteousness is an everlasting righteousness - The word צדק tsedek is a word of very extensive meaning in the Bible. It signifies, not only God's inherent righteousness and perfection of nature, but also his method of treating others; his plan of redemption; his method of saving others. And the word δικαιοσυνη, which answers to it, in the Septuagint and in the New Testament, is used with the same latitude of meaning, and in the same sense; particularly in that remarkable passage, <reference osisRef="Rom.3.25-Rom.3.26">Rom 3:25-26</reference> (note), where see the notes. Thy merciful method of dealing with sinners and justifying the ungodly will last as long as the earth lasts; and thy law that witnesses this, in all its pages, is the truth.
entries.5d22d2af7356bb696d1a99a63b14ca442e2a22fb: <hi type="bold">Verse 143</hi> <div eID="gen22930" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22931" type="x-p"/> Trouble and anguish - I am exercised with various trials from men and devils. <div eID="gen22931" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22932" type="x-p"/> Have taken hold on me - But still I cleave to my God, and am delighted with his law.
entries.a3f453ab2619cc923fe73b063119268b6bc0dfd3: <hi type="bold">Verse 144</hi> <div eID="gen22932" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22933" type="x-p"/> The righteousness of thy testimonies is everlasting - Thy moral law was not made for one people, or for one particular time; it is as imperishable as thy nature, and of endless obligation. It is that law by which all the children of Adam shall be Judged. <div eID="gen22933" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22934" type="x-p"/> Give me understanding - To know and practice it. <div eID="gen22934" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22935" type="x-p"/> And I shall live - Shall glorify thee, and live eternally; not for the merit of having done it, but because thou didst fulfill the work of the law in my heart, having saved me from condemnation by it.
entries.ca36fd20f9d8838560408b03763673541e69c27b: <hi type="bold">Verse 145</hi> <div eID="gen22935" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22936" type="x-p"/> I cried with my whole heart - The whole soul of the psalmist was engaged in this good work. He whose whole heart cries to God will never rise from the throne of grace without a blessing.
entries.5405ea075aaef106b1e3506be3fc2a9fceee3cef: <hi type="bold">Verse 147</hi> <div eID="gen22936" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22937" type="x-p"/> I prevented the dawning - קדמתי kiddamti, "I went before the dawn or twilight."
entries.5456fb247a00cfc1338c4269ed10eab39e564c61: <hi type="bold">Verse 148</hi> <div eID="gen22937" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22938" type="x-p"/> Mine eyes prevent - קדמו kiddemu, "go before the watches." Before the watchman proclaims the hour, I am awake, meditating on thy words. The Jews divided the night into three watches, which began at what we call six o'clock in the evening, and consisted each of four hours. The Romans taught them afterwards to divide it into four watches of three hours each; and to divide the day and night into twelve hours each; wherein different guards of soldiers were appointed to watch. At the proclaiming of each watch the psalmist appears to have risen and performed some act of devotion. For a remarkable custom of our Saxon ancestors, see the note on <reference osisRef="Psa.119.164">Psa 119:164</reference> (note).
entries.211735690b54dbcdb32419e220c52a32153d6e2d: <hi type="bold">Verse 150</hi> <div eID="gen22938" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22939" type="x-p"/> They draw nigh - They are just at hand who seek to destroy me. <div eID="gen22939" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22940" type="x-p"/> They are far from thy law - They are near to all evil, but far from thee.
entries.7b57e4278f76104b6205de35997ad3ea1edaaa3b: <hi type="bold">Verse 151</hi> <div eID="gen22940" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22941" type="x-p"/> Thou art near - As they are near to destroy, so art thou near to save. When the enemy comes in as a flood, the Spirit of the Lord lifts up a standard against him.
entries.d46aa7051b381a6ef071ba82a166ba33ea406c4f: <hi type="bold">Verse 152</hi> <div eID="gen22941" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22942" type="x-p"/> Concerning thy testimonies, I have known of old - קדם ידעתי kedem yedati, "Long ago I have known concerning thy testimonies." Thou hast designed that thy testimonies should bear reference to, and evidence of, those glorious things which thou hast provided for the salvation of men; and that this should be an everlasting testimony. They continue, and Christ is come.
entries.73c2f64cf3fc5f13834ba7b9f52db936e5bd9dda: <hi type="bold">Verse 153</hi> <div eID="gen22942" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22943" type="x-p"/> Consider mine affliction - See mine addiction or humiliation: but the eye of the Lord affects his heart; and therefore he never sees the distresses of his followers without considering their situation, and affording them help.
entries.32fd4d29574390390ea46a2b5c21c006c9692882: <hi type="bold">Verse 154</hi> <div eID="gen22943" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22944" type="x-p"/> Plead my cause - ריבה ריבי ribah ribi. "Be my Advocate in my suit." Contend for us against the Babylonians, and bring us out of our bondage. <div eID="gen22944" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22945" type="x-p"/> According to thy word - Spoken by thy prophets for our comfort and encouragement.
entries.ee350fc9885874627f25d03d06973a50c73c3db3: <hi type="bold">Verse 155</hi> <div eID="gen22945" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22946" type="x-p"/> Salvation is far from the wicked - There is no hope of their conversion. <div eID="gen22946" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22947" type="x-p"/> For they seek not thy statutes - And they who do not seek, shall not find.
entries.afc2f58b8d5f42f9872df02ca5bb96e8bcac32e9: <hi type="bold">Verse 156</hi> <div eID="gen22947" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22948" type="x-p"/> Great are thy tender mercies - They are רבים rabbim, multitudes. They extend to all the wretchednesses of all men.
entries.c9a49a9d16f652676f8033eba05aa82a61a2c7a2: <hi type="bold">Verse 158</hi> <div eID="gen22948" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22949" type="x-p"/> I beheld the transgressors, and was grieved - Literally, I was affected with anguish.
entries.ceb06475b5bed8c86c4127cab0b917ca5c9404a7: <hi type="bold">Verse 160</hi> <div eID="gen22949" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22950" type="x-p"/> Thy word is true from the beginning - ראש rosh, the head or beginning of thy word, is true. Does he refer to the first word in the Book of Genesis, בראשית bereshith, "in the beginning?" The learned reader knows that ראש rash, or raash, is the root in that word. Every word thou hast spoken from the first in Bereshith (Genesis) to the end of the law and prophets, and all thou wilt yet speak, as flowing from the fountain of truth, must be true; and all shall have in due time, their fulfllment. And all these, thy words endure for ever. They are true, and ever will be true.
entries.81fef0350b763bf2ac0db10c310c94fc5e52a265: <hi type="bold">Verse 161</hi> <div eID="gen22950" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22951" type="x-p"/> Princes have persecuted me - This may refer to what was done by prime ministers, and the rulers of provinces, to sour the king against the unfortunate Jews, in order still to detain them in bondage. In reference to David, the plotting against him in Saul's court, and the dangers he ran in consequence of the jealousies of the Philistine lords while he sojourned among them, are well known. <div eID="gen22951" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22952" type="x-p"/> My heart standeth in awe - They had probably offers made them of enlargement or melioration of condition, providing they submitted to some idolatrous conditions; but they knew they had to do with a jealous God; their hearts stood in awe, and they were thereby kept from sin.
entries.13d8856a20293468ef419d01223817809b86356e: <hi type="bold">Verse 162</hi> <div eID="gen22952" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22953" type="x-p"/> As one that findeth great spoil - שלל רב shalal rab. This appears to refer to such spoil as is acquired by stripping the dead in a field of battle, taking the rich garments of the slain chiefs; or it may refer to plunder in general. As God opened his eyes he beheld wonders in his law; and each discovery of this kind was like finding a prize.
entries.e281927d99429b2eaa93610777a608dfd43d70bb: <hi type="bold">Verse 163</hi> <div eID="gen22953" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22954" type="x-p"/> I - abhor lying - Perhaps they might have made the confessions which the Chaldeans required, and by mental reservation have kept an inward firm adherence to their creed; but this, in the sight of the God of truth, must have been lying; and at such a sacrifice they would not purchase their enlargement, even from their captivity.
entries.995231968676e89d1e84d678a6372b4b11e14c59: <hi type="bold">Verse 164</hi> <div eID="gen22954" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22955" type="x-p"/> Seven times a day do I praise thee - We have often seen that seven was a number expressing perfection, completion, etc., among the Hebrews; and that it is often used to signify many, or an indefinite number, see <reference osisRef="Pro.24.16">Pro 24:16</reference>; <reference osisRef="Lev.26.28">Lev 26:28</reference>. And here it may mean no more than that his soul was filled with the spirit of gratitude and praise, and that he very frequently expressed his joyous and grateful feelings in this way. But Rabbi Solomon says this is to be understood literally, for they praised God twice in the morning before reading the decalogue, and once after; twice in the evening before the same reading, and twice after; making in the whole seven times. The Roman Church has prescribed a similar service. <div eID="gen22955" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22956" type="x-p"/> In a manuscript Saxon Homily, Domin. 3, in Quadrag, a.d. 971, I find the following singular directions: - <div eID="gen22956" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22957" type="x-p"/> Every Christian man is commanded that he always his body seven times bless with the sign of Christ's cross. <div eID="gen22957" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22958" type="x-p"/> 1. First, at day-break. <div eID="gen22958" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22959" type="x-p"/> 2. Second time at undern tide, (nine o'clock in the morning). <div eID="gen22959" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22960" type="x-p"/> 3. The third time at midday. <div eID="gen22960" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22961" type="x-p"/> 4. The fourth time at noon-tide. (3 o'clock P.M.) <div eID="gen22961" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22962" type="x-p"/> 5. The fifth time in the evening. <div eID="gen22962" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22963" type="x-p"/> 6. The sixth time at night ere he go to rest. <div eID="gen22963" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22964" type="x-p"/> 7. The seventh time at midnight. A good man would do so if he awoke. <div eID="gen22964" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22965" type="x-p"/> It seems that the sign of the cross was thought sufficient, even without prayer.
entries.443bf67527bf450da04a8ce553f6a73adcd0af35: <hi type="bold">Verse 165</hi> <div eID="gen22965" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22966" type="x-p"/> Great peace have they - They have peace in their conscience, and joy in the Holy Spirit; and <div eID="gen22966" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22967" type="x-p"/> Nothing shall offend - Stumble, or put them out of the way.
entries.14a93788328af80f475fff7c9a5c874de22e2003: <hi type="bold">Verse 166</hi> <div eID="gen22967" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22968" type="x-p"/> Lord, I have hoped - Thou hast promised deliverance, and I have expected it on the ground of that promise.
entries.3c4359d3f63c6bcf639b1f1943e97db88eee6ff9: <hi type="bold">Verse 167</hi> <div eID="gen22968" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22969" type="x-p"/> My soul hath kept - I have not attended to the latter merely, but my spirit has entered into the spirit and design of thy testimonies.
entries.fcdc0616d0919c64b09c177c91d6377931b008ff: <hi type="bold">Verse 168</hi> <div eID="gen22969" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22970" type="x-p"/> For all my ways are before thee - Thou knowest that I do not lie; thy eye has been upon my heart and my conduct, and thou knowest that I have endeavored to walk before thee with a perfect heart.
entries.5885baf84b1e7d90a93d8d03a76081bfbbbbe61c: <hi type="bold">Verse 169</hi> <div eID="gen22970" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22971" type="x-p"/> Let my cry come near before thee - This is really a fine image; it is of frequent occurrence, and is little heeded. Here the psalmists cry for deliverance is personified; made an intelligent being, and sent up to the throne of grace to negotiate in his behalf. He pursues this prosopopoeia in the next verse and sends his supplication in the same way. I have already had occasion to refer to a similar figure in Homer, where prayers are represented as the daughters of Jupiter. See on <reference osisRef="Psa.88.2">Psa 88:2</reference> (note).
entries.a6d9fd00051e95a577b3bdf86aa4415e59ddf1a7: <hi type="bold">Verse 171</hi> <div eID="gen22971" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22972" type="x-p"/> My lips shall utter praise - תהלה tehillah, a song of praise.
entries.353f24a55b547e1f0477d08f58761724b4d376f1: <hi type="bold">Verse 172</hi> <div eID="gen22972" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22973" type="x-p"/> My tongue shall speak of thy word - There is a curious distinction here. In the preceding verse he says, "My lips shall utter;" here no reference is made to articulate sounds, except as affixed to musical notes. In this verse he says, "My tongue shall speak;" here articulate and intelligible words are intended. He first utters sounds connected with words expressive of his grateful feelings; in the second he speaks words, principally those which God himself had spoken, containing promises of support, purposes relative to the redemption of his people, and denunciations against their enemies.
entries.41776b355784b63e26801d21d80ba386b4fbe19b: <hi type="bold">Verse 173</hi> <div eID="gen22973" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22974" type="x-p"/> Let thine hand help me - Exert thy power in my defense.
entries.3f9d8f6173097d963b89e72404f2554bd6e7160c: <hi type="bold">Verse 175</hi> <div eID="gen22974" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22975" type="x-p"/> Let my soul live - Let my life be preserved, and my soul quickened!
entries.217097dc8e327cf995fd45343e3879b1e23b068d: <hi type="bold">Verse 176</hi> <div eID="gen22975" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22976" type="x-p"/> I have gone astray like a lost sheep - A sheep, when it has once lost the flock, strays in such a manner as to render the prospect of its own return utterly hopeless. I have seen them bleating when they have lost the flock, and when answered by the others, instead of turning to the sound, have gone on in the same direction in which they were straying, their bleatings answered by the rest of the flock, till they were out of hearing! This fact shows the propriety of the next clause. <div eID="gen22976" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22977" type="x-p"/> Seek thy servant - I shall never find thee; come to the wilderness, take me up, and carry me to the flock. See the notes on the parable of the lost sheep, <reference osisRef="Luk.15.4">Luk 15:4</reference> (note), etc. The psalmist began with "Blessed are the undefiled in the way, who walk in the law of the Lord;" and he concludes with "I have gone astray like a lost sheep; seek thy servant." And thus, conscious of the blessedness of those who are in the way or righteousness, he desires to be brought into it, that he may walk in newness of life. <reference osisRef="Psa.119.1">Psa 119:1</reference> : "It is a good way, and they are blessed that walk in it." <hi type="bold">Verse </hi>the last, "Bring me into this way, that I may be blessed." And thus the Psalm, in sentiment, returns into itself; and the latter verse is so connected with the former, as to make the whole a perfect circle, like the serpent biting its own tail. <div eID="gen22977" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22978" type="x-p"/> There is one extraordinary perfection in this Psalm: begin where you will, you seem to be at the commencement of the piece; end where you will, you seem to close with a complete sense. And yet it is not like the Book of Proverbs, a tissue of detached sentences; it is a whole composed of many parts, and all apparently as necessary to the perfection of the Psalm, as the different alphabetical letters under which it is arranged are to the formation of a complete alphabet. Though there be a continual recurrence of the same words, which would of itself prevent it from having a pleasing effect upon the ear, yet these words are so connected with a vast variety of others, which show their force and meaning in still new and impressive points of light, that attention is still excited, and devotion kept alive, during the whole reading. It is constructed with admirable art, and every where breathes the justest and highest encomiums on the revelation of God; shows the glories of the God who gave it, the necessities and dependence of his intelligent creatures, the bounty of the Creator, and the praise and obedience which are his due. It is elegant throughout; it is full of beauties, and I have endeavored in the preceding notes to mark some of them; but the number might have been greatly multiplied. To no Psalm can its own words be better applied, <reference osisRef="Psa.119.18">Psa 119:18</reference> : "Open thou mine eyes, that I may behold wondrous things out of thy law."  <chapter eID="Ps.119"/> <div eID="gen22978" type="x-p"/>
