                     <ns0:p n="118">118 Thou hast trodden down all them that err from thy statutes: for their deceit <ns0:hi>is</ns0:hi> falshood <ns0:note n="p" place="bottom">All their crafty and deceitful devices, by which they de<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />sign to ensnare and ruine me and other good men, shall de<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ceive them and their own expectations, and bring that de<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />struction upon themselves which they design for others.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
                     <ns0:p n="119">119 Thou <ns0:note n="†" place="margin">
                           <ns0:hi>Heb.</ns0:hi> causest to cease.</ns0:note> puttest away <ns0:note n="q" place="bottom">Thou removest them from thy presence and from the society of thy people and from the land of the living.</ns0:note> all the wicked of the earth <ns0:hi>like</ns0:hi> dross <ns0:note n="r" place="bottom">Which though for a season it be mixed with gold or silver, is not onely separated from it as an useless and contemptible thing, but also is utterly consumed by fire.</ns0:note>, therefore I love thy testi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />monies <ns0:note n="s" place="bottom">Because they are the best preservatives against wickedness, and against those dread<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ful punishments attending upon it, of which he prosesseth his fear in the next verse.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
                     <ns0:p n="120">120 My flesh trembleth for fear of thee, and I am afraid of thy judgments <ns0:note n="t" place="bottom">The observation of thy terrible judgments against ungod<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ly men, and the conscience of my own infirmity and manifold sins, makes me fear lest thou shouldst punish me also, as thou mightest justly do, if thou shouldst be strict to mark what is amiss in me, or lest I should partake with them in their sins, and consequently in their plagues.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
                  </ns0:div>
                  <ns0:div type="part">
                     <ns0:head>AIN.</ns0:head>
                     <ns0:p n="121">121 I have done judgment and justice <ns0:note n="u" place="bottom">
                           <ns0:hi>i. e.</ns0:hi> Just judgment, as <ns0:hi>Eccles.</ns0:hi> 5. 7. to wit, towards mine oppressors, whom I have no way injured.</ns0:note>: leave me not to mine oppressors.</ns0:p>
                     <ns0:p n="122">122 Be surety for thy servant <ns0:note n="x" place="bottom">Do thou undertake and plead my cause against all mine enemies, as a surety rescues the poor persecuted debtor from the hands of a severe creditor.</ns0:note> for good <ns0:note n="y" place="bottom">For my safety and comfort.</ns0:note>: let not the proud oppress me.</ns0:p>
                     <ns0:p n="123">123 <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Ver. 81. Psal. 123. 1, 2.</ns0:note> Mine eyes fail for thy salvation, and for the word of thy righteousness <ns0:note n="z" place="bottom">For the performance of thy righteous or faithful or mer<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ciful word or promise.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
                     <ns0:p n="124">124 Deal with thy servant according unto thy mercy <ns0:note n="a" place="bottom">Not according to strict justice, nor according to my sins.</ns0:note>, and teach me thy statutes.</ns0:p>
                     <ns0:p n="125">125 I <ns0:hi>am</ns0:hi> thy servant, give me understanding, that I may know thy testimonies.</ns0:p>
                     <ns0:p n="126">126 <ns0:hi>It is</ns0:hi> time <ns0:note n="b" place="bottom">It is high time or a fit season.</ns0:note> for thee, LORD, to work <ns0:note n="b" place="bottom">To put forth thy pow<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />er for the vindication of thy own name and cause, and for the restraint and punishment of evil-doers.</ns0:note>: for they <ns0:note n="c" place="bottom">To wit, mine oppressors, or the wicked; whom it was needless to express, both because they had been lately and frequently mentioned before, and partly because it was evident from the following words.</ns0:note> have made void thy law <ns0:note n="d" place="bottom">Or, <ns0:hi>abrogated thy law,</ns0:hi> have professedly and open<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ly cast off its authority, resolvedly preferring their own wills and lusts before it, trampled upon thy plain commands, and despised both thy promises and thy threatnings. They have not onely sinned through ignorance and infirmity, but pre<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />sumptuously and maliciously.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
                     <ns0:p n="127">127 <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Psal. 19. 10. ver. 72. Prov. 8. 11.</ns0:note> Therefore I love thy commandments <ns0:note n="e" place="bottom">Partly because it is one evidence of their excellency that they are disliked by the vilest of men; partly out of a just indignation and opposition against thy sworn enemies; and partly because the great and general Apostasie of others makes this duty more necessary to prevent their own and other mens relapses.</ns0:note> above gold, yea, above fine gold.</ns0:p>
                     <ns0:p n="128">128 Therefore <ns0:note n="f" place="bottom">For the reasons now mentioned.</ns0:note> I esteem all <ns0:hi>thy</ns0:hi> precepts <ns0:hi>con<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />cerning</ns0:hi> all <ns0:hi>things to be</ns0:hi> right <ns0:note n="g" place="bottom">I do not make void all thy precepts, as they did <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 126. nor yet am I par<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tial in my approbation of them, as others are, who reject all such as are opposite to their lusts and interests; but I ap<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />prove all of them without any exception, and that not onely in my judgment, but in my heart and life, as appears by that hatred of sin which is opposed to it in the next clause.</ns0:note>; <ns0:hi>and</ns0:hi> I hate every false way.</ns0:p>
                  </ns0:div>
                  <ns0:div type="part">
                     <ns0:head>PE.</ns0:head>
                     <ns0:p n="129">129 Thy testimonies <ns0:hi>are</ns0:hi> 
                        <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Ver. 18.</ns0:note> wonderful <ns0:note n="h" place="bottom">In regard of the deep and wonderful mysteries, and most excellent counsels and directions, far exceeding all the rules of the greatest Philosophers, and the exceeding great and precious promises of God contained in them. This is the reason of his high estimation of them expressed in the last verse.</ns0:note>: therefore doth my soul keep them.</ns0:p>
                     <ns0:p n="130">130 The entrance of thy words <ns0:note n="i" place="bottom">The very beginnings and rudiments of it, the first dis<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />coveries of those sacred Mysteries; and much more the depths of them, in which their chief excellency consists. Or, as other both ancient and later Interpreters render the place, <ns0:hi>the opening of thy words,</ns0:hi> by which may be understood either, 1. the opening of mens minds by the Word of God; but that seems to be the same thing with <ns0:hi>giving light,</ns0:hi> which here follows: or, 2. the opening or declaration of Gods mind made in and by his Word.</ns0:note> giveth light: <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Psal. 19. 7.</ns0:note> it giveth understanding unto the sim<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ple <ns0:note n="k" place="bottom">To the most ignorant and un<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />learned persons, who are but willing to learn.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
                     <ns0:p n="131">131 I opened my mouth, and panted <ns0:note n="l" place="bottom">I thirst after thy precepts, and pursue them eagerly, as it were with open mouth, ready and greedy to receive them. It is a Metaphor from one that makes great haste after ano<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ther, whereby he is forced to pant and to open his mouth for air to refresh himself.</ns0:note>: for I longed for thy commandments.</ns0:p>
                     <ns0:p n="132">132 Look thou upon me <ns0:note n="m" place="bottom">To wit, favourably, as the next clause explains it, and as this phrase is commonly used: whereby also he implies that God at present did hide his face and favour from him.</ns0:note>, and be merciful unto me, <ns0:note n="†" place="margin">Heb. <ns0:hi>accord<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ing to the judg<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ment towards those,</ns0:hi> &c.</ns0:note> as thou usest to do unto those that love thy Name <ns0:note n="n" place="bottom">As thou hast done in all former ages. Do not deny me the common priviledge of all the faithful.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
                     <ns0:p n="133">133 Order my steps <ns0:note n="o" place="bottom">By thy grace direct and govern all my motions and acti<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ons.</ns0:note> in thy word <ns0:note n="p" place="bottom">In the way prescribed in thy Word: Or, <ns0:hi>by thy word.</ns0:hi> Let thy Spirit accompany thy Word, and ingraft it within me, so that I may be guided and ruled by it.</ns0:note>: and <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Psal. 19. 13.</ns0:note> let not any iniquity have dominion over me <ns0:note n="q" place="bottom">And although I have evil inclinations and affections within me, let them not bear sway in me, nor withdraw me from the course of obedience.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
                     <ns0:p n="134">134 Deliver me from the oppression of man <ns0:note n="r" place="bottom">As he prayed against the inward impediment of his obe<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />dience, <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 133. so here he prayeth against an external impe<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />diment of it, and a common temptation to sin.</ns0:note>: so will I keep thy precepts.</ns0:p>
                     <ns0:p n="135">135 Make thy face to shine upon thy ser<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />vant <ns0:note n="s" place="bottom">Look upon me with a pleased and favourable counte<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />nance. Comp. <ns0:hi>Numb.</ns0:hi> 6. 25. <ns0:hi>Prov.</ns0:hi> 16. 15.</ns0:note>: and teach me thy statutes.</ns0:p>
                     <ns0:p n="136">136 <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Ver. 53. & 158. Jer. 9. 1. & 14. 17. See Ezek. 9. 4.</ns0:note> Rivers of waters <ns0:note n="t" place="bottom">Plentiful and perpetual tears witnesses of my deep sor<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />row for Gods dishonour and displeasure, and for the miseries which sinners bring upon themselves and others.</ns0:note> run down mine eyes: because they <ns0:note n="u" place="bottom">To wit, the wicked, as before, <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 126. who were not worthy to be mentioned: for this Pronoun is oft used in way of contempt, as <ns0:hi>Luke</ns0:hi> 14. 24. & 19. 27. <ns0:hi>Ioh.</ns0:hi> 7. 11. & 8. 10. <ns0:hi>Acts</ns0:hi> 16. 36.</ns0:note> keep not thy law.</ns0:p>
                  </ns0:div>
                  <ns0:div type="part">
                     <ns0:pb facs="tcp:107763:507" />
                     <ns0:head>TSADDI.</ns0:head>
                     <ns0:p n="137">137 Righteous <ns0:hi>art</ns0:hi> thou <ns0:note n="x" place="bottom">By thine essence and nature, and therefore it is impossi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ble that thou shouldest be unjust in any of thy Laws or Pro<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />vidences.</ns0:note>, O LORD, and up<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />right <ns0:hi>are</ns0:hi> thy judgments.</ns0:p>
                     <ns0:p n="138">138 Thy testimonies <ns0:hi>that</ns0:hi> thou hast comman<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ded <ns0:hi>are</ns0:hi> 
                        <ns0:note n="†" place="margin">
                           <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#APEX" extent="1 word">
                              <ns0:desc>〈◊〉</ns0:desc>
                           </ns0:gap> 
                           <ns0:hi>righte<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />
                              <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#APEX" extent="1+ letters">
                                 <ns0:desc>•…</ns0:desc>
                              </ns0:gap>
                           </ns0:hi>
                        </ns0:note> righteous, and very <ns0:note n="‖" place="margin">
                           <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#APEX" extent="1 word">
                              <ns0:desc>〈◊〉</ns0:desc>
                           </ns0:gap> 
                           <ns0:hi>faith<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />
                              <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#APEX" extent="1+ letters">
                                 <ns0:desc>•…</ns0:desc>
                              </ns0:gap>
                           </ns0:hi>
                        </ns0:note> faithful <ns0:note n="y" place="bottom">But this verse is otherwise rendred by all the ancient In<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />terpreters and by divers others, and that more agreeably to the order of the words in the Hebrew Text, <ns0:hi>Thou hast com<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />manded righteousness</ns0:hi> even <ns0:hi>thy testimonies</ns0:hi> (or, <ns0:hi>the righteousness of thy testimonies,</ns0:hi> or, <ns0:hi>thy righteous testimonies,</ns0:hi> by a common Hebraism, or rather, <ns0:hi>righteousness</ns0:hi> in or by <ns0:hi>thy testimonies,</ns0:hi> no<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />thing being more frequent than the Ellipsis of the prefix <ns0:hi>beth</ns0:hi> which signifies <ns0:hi>in</ns0:hi> or <ns0:hi>by:) and truth</ns0:hi> (or, <ns0:hi>and true,</ns0:hi> thy righ<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />teous and true testimonies: although the other seems to be the better translation) <ns0:hi>earnestly.</ns0:hi> So the sence is, Thou hast strictly and severely, under the highest obligations and pe<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />nalties, commanded in thy Word that men should be just and true in all their actions. And this agrees very well with the next foregoing verse, wherein he affirmed that God is righteous, and doth righteous things; and then here he adds that he requires righteousness and truth from all men.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
                     <ns0:p n="139">139 <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">
                           <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#APEX" extent="1 word">
                              <ns0:desc>〈◊〉</ns0:desc>
                           </ns0:gap> 69. 9. <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#APEX" extent="1 word">
                              <ns0:desc>〈◊〉</ns0:desc>
                           </ns0:gap> 2. 17.</ns0:note> My zeal hath <ns0:note n="†" place="margin">
                           <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#APEX" extent="1 word">
                              <ns0:desc>〈◊〉</ns0:desc>
                           </ns0:gap> 
                           <ns0:hi>cut me</ns0:hi> 
                           <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#APEX" extent="1 word">
                              <ns0:desc>〈◊〉</ns0:desc>
                           </ns0:gap>
                        </ns0:note> consumed me <ns0:note n="z" place="bottom">I am tormented and cut to the heart with grief and an<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ger at it.</ns0:note>: because mine enemies have forgotten thy words <ns0:note n="a" place="bottom">
                           <ns0:hi>i. e.</ns0:hi> Despise and disobey them; which in Scri<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />pture use is oft called a forgetting of them, as the remembring of them is oft put for loving and practising them.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
                     <ns0:p n="140">140 <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">
                           <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#APEX" extent="1 word">
                              <ns0:desc>〈◊〉</ns0:desc>
                           </ns0:gap>. 12. 6. <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#APEX" extent="1 word">
                              <ns0:desc>〈◊〉</ns0:desc>
                           </ns0:gap> 1<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#APEX" extent="1+ letters">
                              <ns0:desc>•…</ns0:desc>
                           </ns0:gap>. 30.</ns0:note> Thy word <ns0:hi>is</ns0:hi> very <ns0:note n="†" place="margin">
                           <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#APEX" extent="1 word">
                              <ns0:desc>〈◊〉</ns0:desc>
                           </ns0:gap>. 30. 5. <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#APEX" extent="1 word">
                              <ns0:desc>〈◊〉</ns0:desc>
                           </ns0:gap> 
                           <ns0:hi>tryed,</ns0:hi> or <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#APEX" extent="1 word">
                              <ns0:desc>〈◊〉</ns0:desc>
                           </ns0:gap>
                        </ns0:note> pure <ns0:note n="b" place="bottom">Without the least mixture of any falshood or sin, both which are frequent in the words or precepts of men.</ns0:note>: therefore <ns0:note n="c" place="bottom">Be<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />cause of that exact purity and holiness of it, for which very reason ungodly men either despise or hate it.</ns0:note> thy servant loveth it.</ns0:p>
                     <ns0:p n="141">141 I <ns0:hi>am</ns0:hi> small <ns0:note n="d" place="bottom">Or, <ns0:hi>a little one,</ns0:hi> not for age, but in respect of my con<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />dition in the world, mean and obscure.</ns0:note> and despised: yet do not I forget thy precepts.</ns0:p>
                     <ns0:p n="142">142 Thy righteousness <ns0:hi>is</ns0:hi> an everlasting righ<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />teousness <ns0:note n="e" place="bottom">Constant and unchangeable, the same in all ages and pla<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ces and to all persons, of eternal truth and justice, never to be dispensed with nor to be made void.</ns0:note>, and thy law <ns0:hi>is</ns0:hi> the truth <ns0:note n="f" place="bottom">Nothing but truth; or, as true as truth it self.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
                     <ns0:p n="143">143 Trouble and anguish <ns0:note n="g" place="bottom">Outward troubles and anguish of spirit: or, great an<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />guish or distress.</ns0:note> have <ns0:note n="†" place="margin">
                           <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#APEX" extent="1 word">
                              <ns0:desc>〈◊〉</ns0:desc>
                           </ns0:gap>. <ns0:hi>
                              <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#APEX" extent="1+ letters">
                                 <ns0:desc>•…</ns0:desc>
                              </ns0:gap>ound</ns0:hi> 
                           <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#APEX" extent="1 word">
                              <ns0:desc>〈◊〉</ns0:desc>
                           </ns0:gap>
                        </ns0:note> taken hold on me: <ns0:hi>yet</ns0:hi> thy commandments <ns0:hi>are</ns0:hi> my delights.</ns0:p>
                     <ns0:p n="144">144 <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">
                           <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#APEX" extent="1+ letters">
                              <ns0:desc>•…</ns0:desc>
                           </ns0:gap>er. 106. <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#APEX" extent="1+ letters">
                              <ns0:desc>•…</ns0:desc>
                           </ns0:gap> 160.</ns0:note> The righteousness of thy testimonies <ns0:hi>is</ns0:hi> everlasting: give me understanding, and I shall live <ns0:note n="h" place="bottom">I shall be kept from those sins which deserve and bring death.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
                  </ns0:div>
                  <ns0:div type="part">
                     <ns0:head>KOPH.</ns0:head>
                     <ns0:p n="145">145 I cried with <ns0:hi>my</ns0:hi> whole heart, hear me, O LORD: I will keep thy statutes.</ns0:p>
                     <ns0:p n="146">146 I cri<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#APEX" extent="1+ letters">
                           <ns0:desc>•…</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap> unto thee, save me, <ns0:note n="‖" place="margin">Or, <ns0:hi>that may</ns0:hi> 
                           <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#APEX" extent="1 word">
                              <ns0:desc>〈◊〉</ns0:desc>
                           </ns0:gap>.</ns0:note> and I shall keep thy testimonies.</ns0:p>
                     <ns0:p n="147">147 <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Psal. 5. 3. & 130. 6.</ns0:note> I prevented the dawning of the mor<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ning <ns0:note n="i" place="bottom">Heb. <ns0:hi>the twilight,</ns0:hi> to wit, of the morning, by compa<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ring <ns0:hi>Psal.</ns0:hi> 88. 13. And so this word is used 1 <ns0:hi>Sam.</ns0:hi> 30. 17.</ns0:note>, and cried: I hoped in thy word.</ns0:p>
                     <ns0:p n="148">148 <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Psal. 63. 1, 6.</ns0:note> Mine eyes prevent the <ns0:hi>night</ns0:hi> watches <ns0:note n="k" place="bottom">Heb. <ns0:hi>the watches;</ns0:hi> which were kept onely by night. And these watches were then three, as hath been more than once observed. And this is not to be understood of the first watch, which was at the beginning of the night, for the pre<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />vention thereof was very easie and frequent and inconsidera<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ble, but of the <ns0:hi>middle watch,</ns0:hi> as it is called <ns0:hi>Iudg.</ns0:hi> 7. 19. which was set in the middle of the night; and especially of the <ns0:hi>morning watch,</ns0:hi> as it is called <ns0:hi>Exod.</ns0:hi> 14. 24. which was set some hours before the dawning of the day: and so this is an aggravation and addition to what he said <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 147.</ns0:note>, that I might meditate in thy word.</ns0:p>
                     <ns0:p n="149">149 Hear my voice according unto thy loving kindness: O LORD, quicken me according to thy judgment <ns0:note n="l" place="bottom">According to thy word, which is oft called Gods <ns0:hi>Iudg<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ment:</ns0:hi> or, according to thy custom or manner of dealing with me and with others of thy people; as this word is taken above <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 132.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
                     <ns0:p n="150">150 They draw nigh <ns0:note n="m" place="bottom">To wit, to me, or against me, as <ns0:hi>Psal.</ns0:hi> 27. 2. they are at hand and ready to seize upon me.</ns0:note> that follow after mis<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />chief: they are far from thy law <ns0:note n="n" place="bottom">They cast away far from them all thoughts of and respect to thy Law, which for<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />bids such wicked practices.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
                     <ns0:p n="151">151 Thou <ns0:hi>art</ns0:hi> near <ns0:note n="o" place="bottom">To me<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> Thou art as ready and present to succour me, as they are to molest me.</ns0:note>, O LORD: and all thy commandments <ns0:note n="p" place="bottom">Considered with the promises and threatnings, which are frequently annexed to them. Or, the promises, as this word seems to be used, <ns0:hi>Psal.</ns0:hi> 111. 7. and elsewhere in this Psalm. And God is said to <ns0:hi>command</ns0:hi> not onely his precepts or the observation thereof, but also his <ns0:hi>Covenant, Psal.</ns0:hi> 105. 8. & 111. 9. which is a collection or body of the promises; and his <ns0:hi>loving kindness, Psal.</ns0:hi> 42. 8. which is the fountain of the promises; and his <ns0:hi>blessing, Psal.</ns0:hi> 133. 3. which is the fruit of his promises; and <ns0:hi>deliverances,</ns0:hi> 44. 4. which are the things promised. And therefore it is not strange if the promises be sometimes called <ns0:hi>Command<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ments.</ns0:hi>
                        </ns0:note> 
                        <ns0:hi>are</ns0:hi> truth.</ns0:p>
                     <ns0:p n="152">152 <ns0:note n="†" place="margin">Heb. <ns0:hi>I knew of old from thy precepts.</ns0:hi> So Gr. ver. 89. Psal. 111. 7. 8.</ns0:note> Concerning thy testimonies, I have known of old <ns0:note n="q" place="bottom">By my own long experience, ever since I arrived at any knowledge in those matters.</ns0:note>, that thou hast founded them for ever <ns0:note n="r" place="bottom">That thou hast established them upon sure and everlasting foundations.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
                  </ns0:div>
                  <ns0:div type="part">
                     <ns0:head>RESH.</ns0:head>
                     <ns0:p n="153">153 Consider mine affliction, and deliver me: for I do not forget thy law.</ns0:p>
                     <ns0:p n="154">154 <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Psal. 35. 1. Mich. 7. 9.</ns0:note> Plead my cause, and deliver me: quick<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />en me according to thy word.</ns0:p>
                     <ns0:p n="155">155 Salvation is far from the wicked: for they seek not thy statutes <ns0:note n="s" place="bottom">And therefore on the contrary I trust that thou wilt save me because I do seek them. My wicked enemies shall cer<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tainly be destroyed, by which means I shall be delivered.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
                     <ns0:p n="156">156 <ns0:note n="‖" place="margin">
                           <ns0:hi>Or,</ns0:hi> many.</ns0:note> Great <ns0:hi>are</ns0:hi> thy tender mercies, O LORD: quicken me according to thy judgments <ns0:note n="t" place="bottom">According to the manner of thy administrations towards thy people, as <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 149.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
                     <ns0:p n="157">157 Many <ns0:hi>are</ns0:hi> my persecutors, and mine ene<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />mies; <ns0:hi>yet</ns0:hi> do I not decline from thy testimo<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />nies <ns0:note n="u" place="bottom">Though they tempt me to do so, and persecute me be<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />cause I will not do it.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
                     <ns0:p n="158">158 I beheld the transgressors <ns0:note n="x" place="bottom">I observed and considered their ungodly courses.</ns0:note>, and was grie<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ved because they kept not thy word.</ns0:p>
                     <ns0:p n="159">159 Consider how <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Ver. 132.</ns0:note> I love thy precepts <ns0:note n="y" place="bottom">Which was the cause of my grief for their violation of them.</ns0:note>: quicken me, O LORD, according to thy loving kindness.</ns0:p>
                     <ns0:p n="160">160 <ns0:note n="†" place="margin">Heb. <ns0:hi>The be<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ginning of thy word</ns0:hi> is <ns0:hi>true.</ns0:hi>
                        </ns0:note> Thy word <ns0:hi>is</ns0:hi> true <ns0:hi>from</ns0:hi> the beginning <ns0:note n="z" place="bottom">Either from the beginning of the world: or ever since thou hast revealed thy mind by thy word to the sons of men, all thy words have been found to be true and certain, and so they will be to the end of the world, as is implied in the next clause. Or, as it is in the margent, <ns0:hi>the beginning</ns0:hi> (or, as others render it, <ns0:hi>the summ,</ns0:hi> as this very word is used, <ns0:hi>Exod.</ns0:hi> 30. 12. <ns0:hi>Numb.</ns0:hi> 26. 2. & 31. 26. to wit, the whole of it, there is not the least part of it, which is not so) <ns0:hi>of thy word is true.</ns0:hi>
                        </ns0:note>: and <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Ver. 89.</ns0:note> every one of thy righteous judgments en<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />dureth for ever.</ns0:p>
                  </ns0:div>
                  <ns0:div type="part">
                     <ns0:pb facs="tcp:107763:508" />
                     <ns0:head>SCHIN.</ns0:head>
                     <ns0:p n="161">161 Princes <ns0:note n="a" place="bottom">Who had power to do it, and who ought to have used their authority to protect me whom they knew to be inno<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />cent and injured.</ns0:note> have persecuted me without a cause: but my heart standeth in awe of thy word <ns0:note n="b" place="bottom">But I feared thine offence and displea<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />sure more than their wrath.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
                     <ns0:p n="162">162 I rejoice at thy word, as one that find<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />eth great spoil.</ns0:p>
                     <ns0:p n="163">163 I hate and abhor lying <ns0:note n="c" place="bottom">Or, <ns0:hi>falshood,</ns0:hi> either 1. in my speech and actions, all hypo crisie and deceit, which is the common practice of mine ene<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />mies and of all godless Politicians: or, 2. in doctrine and worship, as this word seems to be used <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 29. because both there and here it is opposed to Gods <ns0:hi>Law.</ns0:hi>
                        </ns0:note>: <ns0:hi>but</ns0:hi> thy law do I love.</ns0:p>
                     <ns0:p n="164">164 <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Ver. 62.</ns0:note> Seven times <ns0:note n="d" place="bottom">Many times, that definite number being oft taken inde<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />finitely, as <ns0:hi>Levit.</ns0:hi> 26. 28. and elsewhere.</ns0:note> a day do I praise thee: because of thy righteous judgments.</ns0:p>
                     <ns0:p n="165">165 Great peace <ns0:note n="e" place="bottom">Either outward prosperity and happiness, which God in his Law and expresly promised to good men; or at least in<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ward peace, satisfaction and tranquillity of mind, arising from the sence of Gods love to them and watchful care over them in all the concerns of this life and of the next.</ns0:note> have they <ns0:note n="f" place="bottom">Heb. is <ns0:hi>to them,</ns0:hi> or, shall be <ns0:hi>to them;</ns0:hi> for the Verb being not ex<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />pressed, it may be understood either way. Although they may meet with some disturbance, yet <ns0:hi>their end shall be peace,</ns0:hi> as is said <ns0:hi>Psal.</ns0:hi> 37. 37.</ns0:note> which love thy law: and <ns0:note n="†" place="margin">Heb. <ns0:hi>they shall have no stum<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />bling block.</ns0:hi> Prov. 22. 5.</ns0:note> nothing shall offend them <ns0:note n="g" place="bottom">Heb. <ns0:hi>they shall have no stumbling block,</ns0:hi> to wit, such at which they shall stumble and fall into mischief and utter ruine, as ungodly men have, before whom God doth oft lay stumbling blocks or occasions of sin and de<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />struction, as it is affirmed by God himself, <ns0:hi>Ier.</ns0:hi> 6. 21. <ns0:hi>Ezek.</ns0:hi> 3. 20. <ns0:hi>Rom.</ns0:hi> 9. 33. out of <ns0:hi>Isa.</ns0:hi> 8. 14.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
                     <ns0:p n="166">166 <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Gen. 49. 18.</ns0:note> LORD, I have hoped for thy salvation, and done thy commandments <ns0:note n="h" place="bottom">Thus performing the condition which thou hast requi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />red, I justly and confidently hope for thy mercy promised.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
                     <ns0:p n="167">167 My soul hath kept thy testimonies: and I love them exceedingly <ns0:note n="i" place="bottom">I have not onely obeyed thy commands, which an hy<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />pocrite may sometimes and in part do for worldly ends, but I have done it with my very soul and from an hearty love to them.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
                     <ns0:p n="168">168 I have kept thy precepts and thy testimo<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />nies: for <ns0:note n="k" place="bottom">Or, <ns0:hi>because.</ns0:hi> This is added either, 1. as the reason or motive of his obedience, which was the consideration of Gods Omniscience, and his desire to approve himself and his ways to God: or, 2. as a proof and evidence of it. Whereas this and all his former professions of his piety were charged by his enemies with deep hypocrisie, and might seem to sa<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />vour of pride and vain-glory, here in the close of them he makes a solemn appeal to that God, who knew his heart and all his ways, and whether these things were not true and real; which if they were not, he tacitly imprecates Gods judgment upon himself.</ns0:note> all my ways <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">
                           <ns0:hi>Or,</ns0:hi> were.</ns0:note> 
                        <ns0:hi>are</ns0:hi> before thee.</ns0:p>
                  </ns0:div>
                  <ns0:div type="part">
                     <ns0:head>TAU.</ns0:head>
                     <ns0:p n="169">169 Let my cry come near before thee <ns0:note n="l" place="bottom">Which at present thou seemest to <ns0:hi>shut out,</ns0:hi> as the Church complained, <ns0:hi>Lam.</ns0:hi> 3. 8.</ns0:note>, O LORD: give me understanding <ns0:note n="m" place="bottom">Whereby I may both know and perform my duty in all particulars.</ns0:note> according to thy word.</ns0:p>
                     <ns0:p n="170">170 Let my supplication come before thee: deliver me according to thy word.</ns0:p>
                     <ns0:p n="171">171 <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Ver. 7.</ns0:note> My lips shall utter praise, when thou hast taught me thy statutes.</ns0:p>
                     <ns0:p n="172">172 My tongue shall speak <ns0:note n="n" place="bottom">Heb. <ns0:hi>shall pour forth</ns0:hi> freely and abundantly like a foun<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tain.</ns0:note> of thy word <ns0:note n="o" place="bottom">In praise of it, for its righteousness, as it here fol<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />lows, its truth and purity and other excellencies.</ns0:note>, for all thy commandments <ns0:note n="p" place="bottom">Even those which to men of corrupted minds seem harsh and un<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />just.</ns0:note> 
                        <ns0:hi>are</ns0:hi> righteousness.</ns0:p>
                     <ns0:p n="173">173 Let thine hand help me: for <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Josh. 24. 22. Prop. 1. 29.</ns0:note> I have chosen thy precepts <ns0:note n="q" place="bottom">For my guide and companion and chief joy and treasure.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
                     <ns0:p n="174">174 I have longed for thy salvation <ns0:note n="r" place="bottom">Either, 1. for deliverance from my present straits and calamities, that I may serve thee with more freedom, and may glorifie thy Name in a more solemn and publick manner: or, 2. that thou wouldest compleatly save me, not onely from my outward pressures, but also from my sins, from my dulness and deadness in thy service, from all inclinations and tempta<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tions to Apostasie and impiety, and from my other indisposi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tions and corruptions, against which he prayeth in divers parts of this Psalm; and that at last thou wouldest crown me with eternal salvation in thy Kingdom, which it is apparent that <ns0:hi>David</ns0:hi> did believe and expect, and hath been already proved from divers passages of this Book.</ns0:note>, O LORD: and thy law <ns0:hi>is</ns0:hi> my delight.</ns0:p>
                     <ns0:p n="175">175 Let my soul live, and it shall praise thee: and let thy judgments <ns0:note n="s" place="bottom">Either, 1. thy providential dispensations whereby thou judgest and rulest the world, punishing the wicked, and pro<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tecting and delivering the godly. Or, 2. thy word or testi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />monies, as this word most commonly signifies in this Psalm, which are the onely ground of my hope in thy help.</ns0:note> help me.</ns0:p>
                     <ns0:p n="176">176 I <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Isai. 53. 6. Luke 15. 4.</ns0:note> have gone astray like a lost sheep <ns0:note n="t" place="bottom">This is meant either, 1. of sinful errours. I have too often swerved from the path of thy precepts through mine own infirmity or the power of temptation: or, 2. of penal errours. I have been banished by the power and tyranny of mine enemies from all my friends and relations, and, which is far worse, from the place of thy worship and presence, and forced to wander hither and thither, hiding my self in moun<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tains and caves and woods, exposed to a thousand snares and dangers.</ns0:note>
                        <ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> seek thy servant <ns0:note n="u" place="bottom">As the shepherd doth his wandring sheep, and bring me back into thy fold.</ns0:note>: for I do not forget thy com<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />mandments.</ns0:p>
                  </ns0:div>
               </ns0:div>
